native-valve-or-late-prosthetic-valve-en.name: Native valve endocarditis or late prosthetic valve endocarditis (>=12 months post-surgery)

primary_therapy.dose: Ceftriaxone 2g IV q24h + Gentamicin 3mg/kg/day IV q24h or in 3 equally divided doses
Ampicillin 2g IV q4h + Gentamicin 3mg/kg/day IV q24h or in 3 equally divided doses

alternative_therapy.condition: Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity or high risk for MRSA
alternative_therapy.adjunct: +/- Gentamicin 3mg/kg/day IV q24h or in 3 equally divided doses

native-valve-or-late-prosthetic-valve-en.comments: Discuss with the microbiologist for organism-specific therapy and duration. If the patient is acutely ill, add flucloxacillin to ampicillin and gentamicin combination.

right-sided-native-valve-endocarditis-iv.name: Native valve right sided endocarditis or endocarditis in IV illicit drug users

alternative_therapy.condition: Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity or high risk for MRSA

early-prosthetic-valve-or-healthcare-ass.name: Early prosthetic valve endocarditis (<=12 months post-surgery) or healthcare-associated endocarditis

primary_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 30mg/kg/day IV in 2 equally divided doses + Gentamicin 3mg/kg/day IV q24h or in 3 equally divided doses

early-prosthetic-valve-or-healthcare-ass.comments: Contact microbiologist. Early surgical consultation is required. If staphylococcal infection is suspected in prosthetic valves, rifampicin to be added after 3-5 days of starting vancomycin and gentamicin. Rifampicin is a 'Reserve Category' antibiotic (Annex 01).

cied-related-endocarditis.name: Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices related endocarditis (CIED related endocarditis)
cied-related-endocarditis.presentation: Vegetation on leads and/or valves, embolism or systemic infection

primary_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 30mg/kg/day IV in 2 equally divided doses + Gentamicin 3mg/kg/day IV q24h or in 3 equally divided doses

cied-related-endocarditis.comments: Contact microbiologist. Definitive treatment of CIED infection is early and complete extraction of all parts of the system; antibiotic therapy is to be considered as a complement to treat associated systemic infection. Device/tissue should be sent for culture in addition to blood culture.

acute-septic-arthritis-adults-native-joi.name: Acute septic arthritis in adults (native joints)

primary_therapy.adjunct: If high risk of infection with a Gram-negative organism add cefotaxime 2g IV q8h / ceftriaxone 2g IV q24h

primary_therapy.dose: 25-30mg/kg IV loading dose followed by 15-20mg/kg/dose IV q12h

alternative_therapy.dose: 25-30mg/kg IV loading dose followed by 15-20mg/kg/dose IV q12h
10mg/kg/dose IV q12h for 3 doses followed by 10mg/kg/dose IV q24h

alternative_therapy.condition: Adults with high risk of infection with a Gram-negative organism and immediate beta lactam hypersensitivity

acute-septic-arthritis-adults-native-joi.comments: Septic joints should be aspirated to dryness / may require wash out in addition to antibiotics. Initial empirical therapy should ideally be guided by Gram stain results. Risk factors for Gram negative infection includes frailty and old age, recurrent UTI, end stage renal failure, recent abdominal surgery etc. Total 4 weeks of antibiotics with minimum 2 weeks of IV antibiotic is generally recommended. Contact microbiologist.

acute-osteomyelitis-adults.name: Acute osteomyelitis in adults

primary_therapy.adjunct: If an infection with a Gram-negative organism is suspected add cefotaxime 2g IV q8h / ceftriaxone 2g IV q24h

primary_therapy.dose: 25-30mg/kg IV loading dose followed by 15-20mg/kg/dose IV q12h

alternative_therapy.dose: 25-30mg/kg IV loading dose followed by 15-20mg/kg/dose IV q12h
10mg/kg/dose IV q12h for 3 doses followed by 10mg/kg/dose IV q24h

acute-osteomyelitis-adults.comments: Monitor LFT with prolonged (>2 weeks) flucloxacillin therapy. Haematogenous acute osteomyelitis usually needs empirical antibiotic coverage for MRSA. Acute vertebral osteomyelitis can be caused by S. aureus including MRSA, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Gram-negative bacilli and streptococci. For transition from IV to oral therapy and duration of therapy, contact microbiologist.

chronic-osteomyelitis.name: Chronic osteomyelitis
chronic-osteomyelitis.comments: Empirical treatment is not indicated. Obtain biopsy for culture before commencing antimicrobials. Antimicrobial therapy should be guided by susceptibility patterns of culture isolates. Antimicrobial therapy alone is not sufficient without surgical intervention. Contact microbiologist for duration of treatment.

prosthetic-joint-infection.name: Prosthetic joint infection
prosthetic-joint-infection.comments: Empirical treatment is not indicated. Withholding antimicrobials for 2 weeks prior to aspiration/biopsy improves isolation of the pathogen. In cases of acute infection or if the patient is systemically unwell, arrange a blood culture. Contact microbiologist. Multiple intraoperative samples taken using separate instruments for separate sites should be sent for microbiology and histology.

suspected-gonococcal-or-meningococcal-se.name: Suspected Gonococcal or Meningococcal septic arthritis (peripheral joints)

diabetic-foot-osteomyelitis-mild-to-mode.name: Diabetic foot infections complicated with osteomyelitis - mild to moderate

primary_therapy.dose: Clindamycin 600mg IV q6h + Ciprofloxacin 750mg PO q12h

diabetic-foot-osteomyelitis-mild-to-mode.comments: Contact microbiologist if the patient is in sepsis, with a high risk for MRSA or with a history of beta-lactam allergy.

diabetic-foot-osteomyelitis-severe.name: Diabetic foot infections complicated with osteomyelitis - severe infection with systemic sepsis
diabetic-foot-osteomyelitis-severe.presentation: Severe infection with osteomyelitis and systemic sepsis
diabetic-foot-osteomyelitis-severe.comments: Contact microbiologist if the patient is in sepsis, with a high risk for MRSA or with a history of beta-lactam allergy.

community-acquired-acute-bacterial-menin.name: Community acquired acute bacterial meningitis

primary_therapy.adjunct: +/- Vancomycin if high possibility of pneumococcal meningitis

community-acquired-acute-bacterial-menin.comments: Adjunctive dexamethasone therapy is recommended: Dexamethasone IV 8-10mg (child: 0.15mg/kg up to 10mg), starting before or with the first dose of antibiotic, then 6 hourly for 2-4 days. Antibiotic therapy should not be delayed if corticosteroids are not available. Ceftriaxone is preferred over cefotaxime due to lower frequency of administration. Vancomycin should be added when there is a high possibility of pneumococcal meningitis in a critically ill patient with poor response to ceftriaxone/cefotaxime. Ampicillin should be considered when there is a risk of Listeria meningitis in elderly or immunocompromised patients.

meningitis-immunocompromised-patients.name: Meningitis in immunocompromised patients (e.g. severe neutropenia, chronic illnesses, HIV)

primary_therapy.dose: Ampicillin 2g IV q4h + Cefotaxime 2g IV q6h + Vancomycin 30mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses

alternative_therapy.dose: Chloramphenicol 25mg/kg IV q6h + Vancomycin 30mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses

meningitis-immunocompromised-patients.comments: In HIV/AIDS patients, consider the possibility of Cryptococcal meningitis. Contact microbiologist.

base-of-skull-fracture-with-csf-leakage.name: Base of skull fracture with CSF leakage

alternative_therapy.dose: Chloramphenicol 25mg/kg IV q6h + Vancomycin as appropriate

base-of-skull-fracture-with-csf-leakage.comments: Routine antibiotic prophylaxis is not recommended for basilar skull fracture with CSF leakage. Consider pneumococcal vaccine.

healthcare-associated-meningitis-and-ven.name: Healthcare associated meningitis and ventriculitis (e.g. penetrating trauma, post-neurosurgery, CSF shunt infections)

primary_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 30mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses + Ceftazidime 2g IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 30mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses + Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h

healthcare-associated-meningitis-and-ven.comments: Removal of infected shunt with appropriate antimicrobial therapy is the most effective treatment. Intrathecal/intraventricular therapy may be indicated in certain circumstances. Contact microbiologist.

chronic-meningitis.name: Chronic meningitis
chronic-meningitis.comments: Treatment depends on the causative organism. No urgent need for empirical therapy. Contact microbiologist for special investigations and treatment.

meningoencephalitis.name: Meningoencephalitis
meningoencephalitis.presentation: Evidence of focal or diffuse neuropsychological dysfunction with meningitis

primary_therapy.adjunct: + Antibiotic(s) according to the age group and risk factors

meningoencephalitis.comments: Aciclovir should be withdrawn if there is: strong evidence for bacterial meningitis on CSF analysis; no evidence of HSV encephalitis in EEG/MRI; negative CSF HSV PCR.

brain-abscess-and-intracranial-empyema.name: Brain abscess, subdural empyema, cranial epidural abscess, spinal epidural abscess

primary_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 30mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses + Ceftriaxone 2g IV q12h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 30mg/kg/day IV in 2 divided doses + Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

brain-abscess-and-intracranial-empyema.comments: Adequate source control is necessary. It is mandatory to send specimens collected during surgery/guided aspiration for culture and ABST. IV antibiotics for 3-4 weeks if surgical intervention is carried out; IV antibiotics for 6-8 weeks if not. Longer durations recommended in immunocompromised/accompanying osteomyelitis.

mild-diarrhoea.name: Mild diarrhoea
mild-diarrhoea.presentation: Less than 6 unformed stools/day and no fever
mild-diarrhoea.comments: Rehydration. Antibiotic therapy is not recommended.

severe-diarrhoea.name: Severe diarrhoea
severe-diarrhoea.presentation: 6 or more unformed stools per day and/or blood and mucus, fever

primary_therapy.dose: 400mg IV q12h for 3-5 days (if oral not tolerated)

severe-diarrhoea.comments: Treatment with co-trimoxazole or fluoroquinolones may increase the risk of haemolytic uraemic syndrome (HUS). Antibiotic therapy is recommended if cholera is suspected. IV therapy is required only when oral therapy is not tolerated.

travellers-diarrhoea-moderate-to-severe.name: Traveller's diarrhoea - moderate to severe

primary_therapy.dose: 1g PO single dose or 500mg PO q24h for 2-3 days

travellers-diarrhoea-moderate-to-severe.comments: IV therapy is required when oral therapy is not tolerated.

cdiff-first-episode-non-severe.name: C. difficile diarrhoea - first episode, non-severe disease
cdiff-first-episode-non-severe.presentation: WBC less than 15000/uL, less than 5 stools per day, creatinine normal
cdiff-first-episode-non-severe.comments: If possible, stop antibiotics likely to be causing symptoms. Stop antimotility drugs and laxatives. Before starting treatment, send a sample of faeces for detection of C. difficile toxin A and B. If not responding, severe/life threatening disease or recurrent disease, contact microbiologist. The maximum daily dose of PO vancomycin should not exceed 2g.

cdiff-severe-disease.name: C. difficile diarrhoea - severe disease
cdiff-severe-disease.presentation: WBC more than 15000/uL, acute rise in serum creatinine, temperature more than 38.5 degrees C, severe colitis

primary_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 125mg PO q6h for 10 days + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h for 10 days

cdiff-severe-disease.comments: If possible, stop antibiotics likely to be causing symptoms. Before starting treatment, send a sample of faeces for detection of C. difficile toxin A and B. If not responding, contact microbiologist. Fidaxomicin is not currently available in Sri Lanka. The maximum daily dose of PO vancomycin should not exceed 2g.

cdiff-life-threatening-fulminant.name: C. difficile diarrhoea - life threatening/fulminant
cdiff-life-threatening-fulminant.presentation: Hypotension, partial/complete ileus or megacolon, CT evidence of fulminant colitis, lactate more than 5mmol/L

primary_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 500mg PO q6h for 10 days + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h for 10 days

cdiff-life-threatening-fulminant.comments: If possible, stop antibiotics likely to be causing symptoms. Before starting treatment, send a sample of faeces for detection of C. difficile toxin A and B. If not responding, contact microbiologist. Fidaxomicin is not currently available in Sri Lanka. The maximum daily dose of PO vancomycin should not exceed 2g.

suspected-cholera.name: Suspected cholera (adults including pregnant women)

alternative_therapy.condition: If resistance to doxycycline is documented
If resistance to doxycycline is documented
If resistance to doxycycline is documented

suspected-cholera.comments: Antibiotic therapy will reduce the volume and duration of diarrhoea.

otitis-externa-bacterial.name: Otitis externa - bacterial
otitis-externa-bacterial.presentation: Systemic antibiotics indicated for: fever, spread of inflammation to pinna, folliculitis, acute localized otitis externa, infections not responding to topical treatment, patients with comorbidities, immunocompromised

primary_therapy.dose: Ear drops: 3 drops q8h (0.5% neomycin + 0.1% betamethasone)
Ear drops: 3 drops q8h (0.3% ofloxacin/ciprofloxacin/gentamicin + 0.1% betamethasone)
500mg PO q12h (if systemic antibiotics are indicated)

alternative_therapy.dose: Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO q12h +/- Clindamycin 300-450mg PO q6-8h

otitis-externa-bacterial.comments: Gentamicin ear drops should be considered only when there is no perforation of the ear drum. Avoid prolonged use. Local antibiotics can be combined with steroids when there is oedema. Review antibiotics according to culture results. Duration of antibiotics is 5 to 7 days. Patients with severe or recurrent otitis externa should be referred to ENT surgeon.

otitis-externa-malignant.name: Otitis externa - malignant (necrotising)

primary_therapy.dose: 400mg IV q12h + topical therapy as in otitis externa

otitis-externa-malignant.comments: Suspect malignant otitis externa in diabetic or immunocompromised patient with severe earache and refer to an ENT surgeon. Continue treatment for 4-6 weeks. Step down to oral ciprofloxacin with clinical improvement. The possibility of fungal aetiology should be considered when not responding to treatment and bacterial cultures are negative.

otitis-externa-fungal.name: Otitis externa - fungal
otitis-externa-fungal.comments: Send relevant cultures. Refer to an ENT surgeon.

acute-otitis-media-no-recent-antibiotics.name: Acute otitis media - if no antibiotics were used within the last month
acute-otitis-media-no-recent-antibiotics.comments: Treat children less than 2 years. For children more than 2 years and adults, who do not have complications can be observed without antibiotics for 48h. There is no place for topical antibiotics. If complicated or immunocompromised, IV antibiotics should be used.

acute-otitis-media-recent-antibiotics.name: Acute otitis media - if antibiotics were used within last month or poor clinical response after 3 days of amoxicillin
acute-otitis-media-recent-antibiotics.comments: Treat children less than 2 years. For children more than 2 years and adults, who do not have complications can be observed without antibiotics for 48h. If complicated or immunocompromised, IV antibiotics should be used.

otitis-media-with-effusion.name: Otitis media with effusion
otitis-media-with-effusion.comments: Antibiotics are not required. Often bilateral and without pain. Most commonly due to viruses or allergies. Refer to an ENT surgeon if persistent.

csom-chronic-mucoid-type-safe.name: Chronic suppurative otitis media - chronic mucoid type (Safe CSOM)
csom-chronic-mucoid-type-safe.comments: Aural toilet is very important. In acute exacerbations, may have to use culture guided oral antibiotics. Intravenous antibiotics may be required if severe and not responding to oral antibiotics. Surgical intervention is essential. Refer to an ENT surgeon. Chloramphenicol ear drops should be avoided unless essential due to irritant effects.

csom-chronic-squamous-type-cholesteatoma.name: Chronic suppurative otitis media - chronic squamous type (Cholesteatoma)
csom-chronic-squamous-type-cholesteatoma.comments: Aural toilet is very important. In acute exacerbations, may have to use culture guided oral antibiotics. Surgical intervention is essential. Refer to an ENT surgeon. Chloramphenicol ear drops should be avoided unless essential due to irritant effects.

mastoiditis-uncomplicated-acute.name: Mastoiditis - uncomplicated acute

alternative_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 1g IV q12h + Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO q12h

mastoiditis-uncomplicated-acute.comments: Patient should be referred to an ENT surgeon. Switch to oral treatment with clinical response.

mastoiditis-complicated.name: Mastoiditis - complicated (e.g. mastoid abscess, intracranial extension, facial palsy)
mastoiditis-complicated.presentation: Mastoid abscess, intracranial extension, facial palsy

alternative_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 1g IV q12h + Ciprofloxacin 500mg PO q12h

mastoiditis-complicated.comments: Empirical therapy may depend on the extent/severity of the infection. Contact microbiologist for empirical antibiotic therapy. Refer to an ENT surgeon for surgical intervention. Antibiotic therapy should be reviewed with culture and ABST results.

acute-bacterial-sinusitis-no-recent-anti.name: Acute bacterial sinusitis - if no antibiotics were used within the last month
acute-bacterial-sinusitis-no-recent-anti.comments: Viruses are the most common causes of acute sinusitis. Antibiotic therapy is not indicated for acute allergic rhinosinusitis. Acute bacterial sinusitis should be considered when symptoms persist for 10 or more days with no improvement/systemically unwell. Parenteral antibiotic therapy is required only for severe/complicated cases.

acute-bacterial-sinusitis-recent-antibio.name: Acute bacterial sinusitis - if antibiotics were used within last month or no response to amoxicillin in 48 hours
acute-bacterial-sinusitis-recent-antibio.comments: Parenteral antibiotic therapy is required only for severe/complicated cases.

chronic-sinusitis.name: Chronic sinusitis
chronic-sinusitis.comments: Antibiotics are usually not effective. Topical steroids/nasal drops/sprays are the mainstay of treatment. Treat acute exacerbations as acute sinusitis. Steroid nasal sprays and surgery are mainstay of treatment. Refer to an ENT surgeon for assessment/surgical intervention.

fungal-sinusitis-allergic.name: Fungal sinusitis - allergic fungal rhinosinusitis
fungal-sinusitis-allergic.comments: Antibiotics are not effective. Refer to an ENT surgeon. Surgical treatment is indicated in all types of fungal sinusitis.

fungal-sinusitis-fungal-ball-invasive.name: Fungal sinusitis - fungal ball, invasive fungal sinusitis
fungal-sinusitis-fungal-ball-invasive.comments: Antibiotics are not effective. Refer to an ENT surgeon. Contact mycologist/microbiologist for antifungal therapy. Need appropriate sampling for fungal cultures.

nasal-vestibulitis-severe.name: Nasal vestibulitis - severe

primary_therapy.dose: Flucloxacillin 500mg IV q6h + Fusidic acid cream local application q12h-q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: Clindamycin 300-450mg PO q6-8h or 900mg IV q8h + Fusidic acid cream local application q12h-q8h

nasal-vestibulitis-severe.comments: Commence treatment as early as possible. Refer to an ENT surgeon. Contact microbiologist if not responding to initial therapy.

nasal-septal-abscess.name: Nasal septal abscess
nasal-septal-abscess.comments: Surgical intervention is essential as early as possible. Refer to an ENT surgeon. Contact microbiologist if not responding to initial therapy.

acute-bacterial-tonsillitis-pharyngitis.name: Acute bacterial tonsillitis/pharyngitis
acute-bacterial-tonsillitis-pharyngitis.presentation: As most pharyngitis are of viral origin, antibiotic treatment is not usually indicated. Associated cough, rhinorrhoea, hoarseness and/or oral ulcers suggest viral aetiology
acute-bacterial-tonsillitis-pharyngitis.comments: Five days may be enough for symptomatic cure; but a 10-day course may increase the chance of microbiological cure.

acute-bacterial-tonsillitis-pharyngitis-.name: Acute bacterial tonsillitis/pharyngitis not responding to oral therapy
acute-bacterial-tonsillitis-pharyngitis-.comments: Step down to oral therapy with clinical improvement. Total duration - 10 days.

peritonsillar-abscess.name: Peritonsillar abscess

primary_therapy.dose: Benzylpenicillin 2MU IV q6h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
Cefuroxime 750mg IV q8h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

peritonsillar-abscess.comments: Surgical intervention is essential. Refer to an ENT surgeon. Step down to oral therapy after surgery with clinical improvement. Total duration - 10 days. Contact microbiologist if not responding to initial therapy.

retropharyngeal-parapharyngeal-abscess.name: Retropharyngeal / parapharyngeal abscess
retropharyngeal-parapharyngeal-abscess.source_control: Early surgical intervention and airway management are essential

primary_therapy.dose: Ceftriaxone 1-2g IV q24h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: Clindamycin 900mg IV q8h + Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h

retropharyngeal-parapharyngeal-abscess.comments: Early surgical intervention and airway management are essential. Refer to an ENT surgeon. Step down to oral therapy after surgery with clinical improvement. Contact microbiologist if not responding to initial therapy.

acute-laryngitis.name: Acute laryngitis
acute-laryngitis.comments: Antibiotic treatment is generally not indicated as most cases are of viral aetiology. Voice rest for 7-10 days. If symptoms persist for more than 48hrs (voice change and pain) treat as acute bacterial tonsillitis.

acute-epiglottitis.name: Acute epiglottitis

alternative_therapy.dose: Clindamycin 900mg IV q8h + Levofloxacin 750mg IV q24h

acute-epiglottitis.comments: Contact ENT surgeon and microbiologist immediately. Urgent surgical intervention/intubation needed for paediatric patients. Step down to oral therapy after surgery with clinical improvement. Levofloxacin is a 'Reserve Category' antibiotic (Annex 01).

suppurative-jugular-thrombophlebitis-lem.name: Suppurative jugular thrombophlebitis (Lemierre's syndrome)

primary_therapy.dose: Ceftriaxone 2g IV q24h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

suppurative-jugular-thrombophlebitis-lem.comments: Refer to an ENT surgeon and microbiologist. Step down to oral therapy with clinical improvement. Duration 3-6 weeks.

conjunctivitis.name: Conjunctivitis
conjunctivitis.presentation: Most cases are viral. Bacterial conjunctivitis is usually unilateral and self-limiting (suspect when the discharge is purulent or if there is associated naso lacrimal duct obstruction). Treat only if severe.

primary_therapy.dose: 0.5% eye drops q6h - bathe/clean eyelids regularly to remove crusting. Continue for 48 hours after resolution.
1% eye ointment applied q6-8h - bathe/clean eyelids regularly to remove crusting. Continue for 48 hours after resolution.

alternative_therapy.condition: Allergic to chloramphenicol or poor compliance with frequent instillation
Allergic to chloramphenicol or poor compliance with frequent instillation

conjunctivitis.comments: Send eye discharge swab for Gram stain and culture prior to treatment if a bacterial infection is suspected. Advise meticulous hand washing and avoid sharing of personal items. Do not wear contact lenses until 24 hours after treatment is completed and all symptoms resolved. Topical steroids are contraindicated.

gonococcal-ophthalmia-neonatorum.name: Gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum

primary_therapy.dose: 100mg/kg IV/IM single dose (may be preferred due to risk of increasing bilirubin levels with ceftriaxone)

gonococcal-ophthalmia-neonatorum.comments: Take conjunctival swabs for Gram staining and special culture for Neisseria species. Topical antimicrobials are not recommended. Treat mother and her sexual partner. Consider Chlamydia trachomatis infection.

chlamydial-conjunctivitis.name: Chlamydial conjunctivitis

primary_therapy.dose: For neonates: erythromycin syrup 12.5mg/kg PO q6h for 14 days

alternative_therapy.dose: 500mg PO q6h for 7 days / 500mg PO q12h for 14 days

chlamydial-conjunctivitis.comments: If Chlamydia trachomatis is suspected send conjunctival scrapings for testing. Contact microbiologist.

endogenous-endophthalmitis-bacterial.name: Endogenous endophthalmitis - bacterial (results from bacteraemia seeding the eye)

primary_therapy.dose: Intravitreal: vancomycin 1mg + ceftazidime 2.25mg / amikacin 0.4mg. Topical: ciprofloxacin 0.3% eye drops hourly + teicoplanin 1% eye drops hourly. Systemic: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h / ceftazidime 2g IV q8h + teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h (3 doses) then 400mg q24h

alternative_therapy.dose: Intravitreal: amikacin 0.4mg + clindamycin 1.0mg. Systemic: vancomycin 1g IV q12h + ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h

endogenous-endophthalmitis-bacterial.comments: Ophthalmic emergency. Immediate ophthalmology referral is needed. Immediate vitrectomy may be needed. Vitreous tap/biopsy should be sent for microscopy and culture. Treatment of the underlying source of bacteraemia with systemic antibiotics is necessary. Contact microbiologist. Each intravitreal agent diluted in 0.1ml of sterile water or normal saline (may need to repeat in 2-3 days). Note the risk of retinal microvasculitis with intravitreal amikacin.

endogenous-endophthalmitis-suspected-fun.name: Endogenous endophthalmitis - suspected fungal infection

primary_therapy.dose: Intravitreal: amphotericin B 5 micrograms in 0.1ml sterile water stat and repeat after 48h if needed. Systemic: fluconazole 400-800mg IV q24h
Intravitreal: voriconazole 100 micrograms in 0.1ml sterile water. Systemic: fluconazole 400-800mg IV q24h

endogenous-endophthalmitis-suspected-fun.comments: Systemic antifungals should be continued for a minimum of 6 weeks based on antifungal susceptibility. Contact microbiologist/mycologist. Preparation of amphotericin B/voriconazole solutions for intravitreal use should be done under strict aseptic conditions.

exogenous-endophthalmitis.name: Exogenous endophthalmitis (post-operative, post-intravitreal injection, bleb-related)
exogenous-endophthalmitis.presentation: Post-operative endophthalmitis (post-cataract surgery) occurs within 1-7 days. Post-intravitreal injection typically presents within 5 days. Bleb-related infection may occur immediately after or months to years following glaucoma surgery.

primary_therapy.dose: Intravitreal: vancomycin 1mg + ceftazidime 2.25mg / amikacin 0.4mg. Topical: ciprofloxacin 0.3% eye drops hourly + teicoplanin 1% eye drops hourly. Systemic: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h / ceftazidime 2g IV q8h + teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h (3 doses) then 400mg q24h

alternative_therapy.dose: Intravitreal: vancomycin 1mg + ciprofloxacin 0.2mg with topical and systemic therapy as in primary therapy

exogenous-endophthalmitis.comments: Immediate ophthalmology referral is needed. Immediate vitrectomy may be needed. Vitreous tap/biopsy should be sent for microscopy and culture. If fungal endophthalmitis is suspected see endogenous endophthalmitis section above for antifungal therapy. Contact microbiologist/mycologist.

penetrating-ocular-trauma-at-risk-of-end.name: Penetrating ocular trauma at risk of getting endophthalmitis

primary_therapy.dose: Intravitreal: ceftazidime 2.25mg / amikacin 0.4mg + moxifloxacin (preservative free) off label use. Systemic: vancomycin 1g IV q12h + ceftazidime 1-2g IV q8h

alternative_therapy.condition: Severe cases, probable intraocular foreign body or anaerobic bacteria
alternative_therapy.dose: Clindamycin 300mg IV q8h + Gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h

penetrating-ocular-trauma-at-risk-of-end.comments: Immediate ophthalmology referral is needed. Systemic antifungal treatment is recommended for suspected fungal infections. Contact microbiologist/mycologist.

suspected-viral-keratitis-herpes-simplex.name: Suspected viral keratitis - herpes simplex virus

primary_therapy.dose: Aciclovir 400mg PO 5 times per day for 7 days + aciclovir 3% eye ointment topically 5 times per day for 14 days or for at least 3 days after healing

alternative_therapy.dose: Aciclovir 400mg PO 5 times per day for 7 days + ganciclovir 0.15% gel 1 drop 5 times per day until healing then q8h for 7 days

suspected-viral-keratitis-herpes-simplex.comments: An immediate ophthalmology referral is needed.

herpes-zoster-ophthalmicus.name: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus with or without keratitis

primary_therapy.dose: Aciclovir 800mg PO 5 times per day for 7 days + topical aciclovir 3% 5 times per day for 14 days

alternative_therapy.dose: Aciclovir 800mg PO 5 times per day for 7 days + topical ganciclovir 0.15% gel 1 drop 5 times per day until healing then three times per day for 7 days

herpes-zoster-ophthalmicus.comments: An immediate ophthalmology referral is needed.

suspected-bacterial-keratitis.name: Suspected bacterial keratitis

primary_therapy.dose: Gatifloxacin 0.3% / moxifloxacin 0.5% eye drops hourly + tobramycin 0.3% eye drops hourly (intensive therapy)

suspected-bacterial-keratitis.comments: An immediate ophthalmology referral is needed. Send scrapings of the ulcer base for bacterial and fungal culture before starting treatment.

contact-lens-associated-bacterial-kerati.name: Contact lens associated bacterial keratitis

primary_therapy.dose: Gatifloxacin 0.3% / moxifloxacin 0.5% eye drops hourly + tobramycin 0.3% eye drops hourly (intensive therapy)

contact-lens-associated-bacterial-kerati.comments: An immediate ophthalmology referral is needed. Send scrapings of the ulcer base for bacterial and fungal culture before starting treatment. Contact lens and storage solution can be sent for microscopy and culture.

suspected-fungal-keratitis.name: Suspected fungal keratitis

primary_therapy.dose: 0.5% eye drops, 1 drop every 1-2 hourly for 3-5 days; then 1 drop 3-4 hourly for 6 weeks

alternative_therapy.dose: 0.15% eye drops, 1 drop 1-2 hourly; tail off according to response
1% eye drops, 1 drop 1-2 hourly; tail off according to response

suspected-fungal-keratitis.comments: An immediate ophthalmology referral is needed. Contact mycologist/microbiologist. Send scrapings of the ulcer base for bacterial and fungal culture before starting treatment.

blepharitis-meibomian-abscess-stye.name: Blepharitis, meibomian abscess (internal hordeolum) and stye (external hordeolum)
blepharitis-meibomian-abscess-stye.presentation: Blepharitis (inflammation of lid margins), meibomian abscess (internal hordeolum), stye (external hordeolum)

primary_therapy.adjunct: Lid hygiene with gentle eyelid scrubs. Surgical treatment +/- flucloxacillin 500mg PO q6h for 5 days
Lid hygiene with gentle eyelid scrubs. Surgical treatment +/- flucloxacillin 500mg PO q6h for 5 days

blepharitis-meibomian-abscess-stye.comments: Acanthamoeba infection must be excluded. Hot packs are adequate for external hordeolum. Role of topical antibiotics is unclear.

orbital-post-septal-cellulitis.name: Orbital (post-septal) cellulitis
orbital-post-septal-cellulitis.presentation: Infection of the tissues posterior to the orbital septum, including the fat and muscle within the bony orbit

primary_therapy.dose: Flucloxacillin 2g IV q6h + Cefotaxime 2g IV q8h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
primary_therapy.adjunct: Switch to co-amoxiclav 625mg PO q8h when clinically appropriate

primary_therapy.dose: Flucloxacillin 2g IV q6h + Ceftriaxone 2g IV q24h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
primary_therapy.adjunct: Switch to co-amoxiclav 625mg PO q8h when clinically appropriate

alternative_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 1g IV q8-12h + Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
Teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h (3 doses) then 400mg q24h + Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

orbital-post-septal-cellulitis.comments: Immediate ophthalmology referral is needed. If MRSA is suspected replace flucloxacillin with vancomycin/teicoplanin. Contact microbiologist.

periorbital-pre-septal-cellulitis-with-e.name: Periorbital (pre-septal) cellulitis - with evidence of external involvement
periorbital-pre-septal-cellulitis-with-e.presentation: Infection of skin and soft tissue around the eye anterior to the orbital septum, with evidence of external involvement

primary_therapy.dose: Co-amoxiclav 625mg PO q8h + Clindamycin 600mg PO q8h
If severe: Co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV q8h + Clindamycin 600mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: 200mg PO loading dose followed by 100mg PO q12h
Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + Clindamycin 600mg IV q8h

periorbital-pre-septal-cellulitis-with-e.comments: Always suspect orbital (post-septal) cellulitis unless there is a clear cause for pre-septal cellulitis. Ophthalmology referral is needed. If MRSA is suspected replace flucloxacillin with vancomycin/teicoplanin. Contact microbiologist in severe infections. Switch to oral therapy with clinical improvement. Total duration - 7 days. For children, immediate ophthalmology referral is needed.

periorbital-pre-septal-cellulitis-withou.name: Periorbital (pre-septal) cellulitis - without evidence of external involvement (with evidence of underlying sinusitis)
periorbital-pre-septal-cellulitis-withou.presentation: Without evidence of external involvement (with evidence of underlying sinusitis)
periorbital-pre-septal-cellulitis-withou.comments: Always suspect orbital (post-septal) cellulitis unless there is a clear cause for pre-septal cellulitis. Contact microbiologist in severe infections or beta-lactam allergy.

acute-uncomplicated-appendicitis.name: Acute uncomplicated appendicitis (no perforation, abscess, or peritonitis)
acute-uncomplicated-appendicitis.comments: In the absence of perforation antibiotic therapy is limited to surgical prophylaxis.

acute-uncomplicated-appendicitis-surgery.name: Acute uncomplicated appendicitis when surgery is not feasible (Appendicolith excluded)

primary_therapy.dose: Cefuroxime 1.5g IV q8h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

acute-uncomplicated-appendicitis-surgery.comments: Specimens collected during surgery should be sent for culture and ABST. If the patient is with sepsis or septic shock, consider starting a carbapenem empirically. Contact microbiologist.

acute-peritonitis-perforated-viscus.name: Acute peritonitis secondary to perforated viscus
acute-peritonitis-perforated-viscus.presentation: Severe abdominal pain, guarding, rigidity, signs of sepsis/peritoneal irritation
acute-peritonitis-perforated-viscus.source_control: Urgent exploratory laparotomy, repair/resection of perforation, peritoneal lavage and drainage

primary_therapy.dose: Ceftriaxone 2g IV once daily (or 1g IV q12h) PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
primary_therapy.adjunct: If critically ill/septic shock: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h (or Meropenem 1g IV q8h if high risk of ESBL)

alternative_therapy.dose: Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
alternative_therapy.adjunct: Add Amikacin 15mg/kg IV once daily if critically ill and renal function permits

acute-peritonitis-perforated-viscus.comments: Obtain peritoneal fluid/pus for Gram stain, aerobic and anaerobic culture before starting antibiotics. Re-evaluate antimicrobial therapy at 48-72 hours based on clinical response and culture results. Total duration 4-7 days if source control is adequate.

acute-cholecystitis-cholangitis.name: Acute cholecystitis and acute cholangitis
acute-cholecystitis-cholangitis.presentation: Fever, right upper quadrant pain, Murphy's sign, jaundice (in cholangitis)
acute-cholecystitis-cholangitis.source_control: Emergency biliary decompression (ERCP or percutaneous drainage) in severe cholangitis; cholecystectomy for cholecystitis

primary_therapy.dose: Ceftriaxone 2g IV once daily PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

acute-cholecystitis-cholangitis.comments: Send blood cultures before initiating therapy. In mild acute cholecystitis, stop antibiotics within 24 hours of successful cholecystectomy if no perforation or gangrene.

intra-abdominal-abscess.name: Intra-abdominal abscess
intra-abdominal-abscess.presentation: Prolonged fever, localized abdominal tenderness, leukocytosis
intra-abdominal-abscess.source_control: Image-guided percutaneous drainage or surgical evacuation of collections

primary_therapy.dose: Ceftriaxone 2g IV once daily PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
primary_therapy.adjunct: Switch to Meropenem 1g IV q8h if post-operative, healthcare-associated, or critically ill

alternative_therapy.dose: Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

intra-abdominal-abscess.comments: Drainage is the definitive therapy. Continue antibiotics until drainage stops, resolution of fever, and normalization of inflammatory markers.

community-acquired-pneumonia-mild.name: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) - Mild
community-acquired-pneumonia-mild.presentation: CURB-65 score 0 or 1, cough, fever, localized chest signs, no hemodynamic compromise

alternative_therapy.dose: Clarithromycin 500mg oral q12h (or Azithromycin 500mg oral once daily) for 5 days
Doxycycline 200mg stat then 100mg oral once daily for 5 days

community-acquired-pneumonia-mild.comments: Suitable for outpatient management. Emphasize review if symptoms worsen within 48 hours.

community-acquired-pneumonia-moderate.name: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) - Moderate
community-acquired-pneumonia-moderate.presentation: CURB-65 score 2, tachypnea more than 30/min, confusion, BUN elevated, age 65 or above

primary_therapy.dose: Co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV q8h (or oral 625mg q8h) PLUS Clarithromycin 500mg oral/IV q12h

community-acquired-pneumonia-moderate.comments: Inpatient admission indicated. Switch from IV to oral route once patient is clinically stable, afebrile for 24-48 hours, and tolerating oral intake.

community-acquired-pneumonia-severe.name: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) - Severe / ICU
community-acquired-pneumonia-severe.presentation: CURB-65 score 3-5, shock, respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation, multilobar infiltrates

primary_therapy.dose: Ceftriaxone 2g IV once daily (or Co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV q8h) PLUS Clarithromycin 500mg IV q12h
primary_therapy.adjunct: If risk factors for Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h PLUS Levofloxacin 750mg IV q24h

alternative_therapy.dose: Levofloxacin 750mg IV q24h PLUS Vancomycin 15-20mg/kg IV q12h (if MRSA suspected)

community-acquired-pneumonia-severe.comments: Obtain blood cultures and sputum/endotracheal aspirate for microbiological investigation before antimicrobial administration. Test for Legionella and pneumococcal urinary antigens if available.

hospital-acquired-pneumonia.name: Hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) and Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
hospital-acquired-pneumonia.presentation: New or progressive lung infiltrate occurring more than 48 hours after admission/intubation, purulent sputum, worsening oxygenation

primary_therapy.dose: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h (extended infusion over 3-4 hours)
primary_therapy.adjunct: Substitute with Meropenem 1g IV q8h if high local prevalence of ESBL or septic shock

alternative_therapy.dose: Levofloxacin 750mg IV q24h PLUS Amikacin 15-20mg/kg IV q24h

hospital-acquired-pneumonia.comments: Add Vancomycin (15-20mg/kg IV q8-12h with therapeutic drug monitoring) if MRSA risk factors or local prevalence more than 20%. Duration of therapy 7 days for responding patients.

empyema-thoracis-lung-abscess.name: Empyema thoracis and Lung abscess
empyema-thoracis-lung-abscess.presentation: Persistent fever, pleuritic chest pain, pleural effusion on imaging with pH less than 7.2 or frank pus
empyema-thoracis-lung-abscess.source_control: Urgent intercostal tube drainage or video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS)

primary_therapy.adjunct: Or Ceftriaxone 2g IV once daily PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: Clindamycin 600mg IV q8h PLUS Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h

empyema-thoracis-lung-abscess.comments: Antibiotic therapy alone is insufficient for empyema without complete pleural evacuation. Therapy often required for 2-4 weeks guided by drainage and clinical resolution.

acute-uncomplicated-cystitis.name: Acute uncomplicated cystitis in women
acute-uncomplicated-cystitis.presentation: Dysuria, urinary frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort, absence of fever or flank pain
acute-uncomplicated-cystitis.comments: Avoid Nitrofurantoin if eGFR less than 30 mL/min or in pyelonephritis due to poor renal tissue penetration. Urine culture not routinely required in first presentation of uncomplicated cystitis.

acute-pyelonephritis-non-severe.name: Acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis (Non-severe)
acute-pyelonephritis-non-severe.presentation: Fever, chills, costovertebral angle tenderness, nausea/vomiting, pyuria, tolerating oral fluids

alternative_therapy.dose: Cefixime 400mg oral once daily for 10 days

acute-pyelonephritis-non-severe.comments: Send urine culture and sensitivity in all cases. Review sensitivities at 48 hours and tailor therapy accordingly.

acute-pyelonephritis-severe-urosepsis.name: Severe acute pyelonephritis and Urosepsis
acute-pyelonephritis-severe-urosepsis.presentation: High fever, rigors, flank pain, hemodynamic instability, elevated lactate, oliguria
acute-pyelonephritis-severe-urosepsis.source_control: Urgent imaging to rule out urinary tract obstruction; emergency nephrostomy or JJ stent if obstructed

primary_therapy.dose: Gentamicin 5-7mg/kg IV once daily PLUS Ampicillin 1g IV q6h
Ceftriaxone 2g IV once daily (if renal impairment precludes aminoglycosides)
primary_therapy.adjunct: Meropenem 1g IV q8h if septic shock or history of ESBL-producing organism

alternative_therapy.dose: Amikacin 15mg/kg IV once daily (or Aztreonam 2g IV q8h if available)

acute-pyelonephritis-severe-urosepsis.comments: Relief of obstruction is an emergency and supersedes antimicrobial efficacy alone. Monitor renal function and aminoglycoside therapeutic levels if multi-day dosing needed.

cellulitis-erysipelas-mild-moderate.name: Cellulitis and Erysipelas (Mild to Moderate)
cellulitis-erysipelas-mild-moderate.presentation: Spreading erythema, warmth, localized pain, edema, distinct anatomical border
cellulitis-erysipelas-mild-moderate.comments: Mark advancing margin with surgical skin marker to assess response. Elevate the affected limb. Address underlying predisposing factors (tinea pedis, venous insufficiency, lymphoedema).

necrotizing-fasciitis.name: Necrotizing fasciitis and severe necrotizing soft tissue infections
necrotizing-fasciitis.presentation: Severe pain out of proportion to skin findings, skin necrosis, bullae, crepitus, rapid progression, septic shock
necrotizing-fasciitis.source_control: Immediate emergent radical surgical debridement of all necrotic fascia and muscle; repeat inspection in 24 hours

primary_therapy.dose: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h PLUS Clindamycin 900mg IV q8h PLUS Vancomycin 15-20mg/kg IV q8-12h
primary_therapy.adjunct: Clindamycin acts as a toxin synthesis inhibitor for Group A Streptococcus and Staphylococcus aureus

primary_therapy.dose: Meropenem 1g IV q8h PLUS Clindamycin 900mg IV q8h PLUS Vancomycin 15-20mg/kg IV q12h

alternative_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 15-20mg/kg IV q12h PLUS Amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

necrotizing-fasciitis.comments: Surgical consultation MUST NOT be delayed for diagnostic imaging or laboratory confirmation. Clindamycin should be continued until patient is afebrile and hemodynamically stable.

diabetic-foot-infection-moderate-severe.name: Diabetic foot infection (Moderate to Severe)
diabetic-foot-infection-moderate-severe.presentation: Ulcer probing to bone, erythema more than 2cm, deep abscess, systemic inflammatory manifestations
diabetic-foot-infection-moderate-severe.source_control: Surgical debridement of slough/necrotic tissue, probe-to-bone evaluation, drainage of plantar abscesses, pressure off-loading

primary_therapy.adjunct: Add Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h if Pseudomonas suspected

primary_therapy.dose: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q8h (for severe limb-threatening infection)

alternative_therapy.dose: Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h PLUS Clindamycin 600mg IV q8h

diabetic-foot-infection-moderate-severe.comments: Obtain deep tissue biopsy/curettage for microbiology after debridement; avoid superficial swab cultures. Plain X-ray/MRI of foot to assess for osteomyelitis.

sepsis-unknown-focus-community.name: Sepsis / Septic shock with unknown focus (Community-acquired)
sepsis-unknown-focus-community.presentation: qSOFA 2 or more or SOFA score increase 2 or more, hypotension, hyperlactataemia, tachypnoea, no localized focus identified

primary_therapy.dose: Ceftriaxone 2g IV stat PLUS Gentamicin 5-7mg/kg IV stat (single dose)
primary_therapy.adjunct: If septic shock: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h (or Meropenem 1g IV q8h if prior ESBL colonization)

alternative_therapy.dose: Levofloxacin 750mg IV q24h PLUS Vancomycin 15-20mg/kg IV q12h

sepsis-unknown-focus-community.comments: Administer intravenous antimicrobials within 1 hour of recognition of sepsis. Draw at least 2 sets of blood cultures prior to therapy. Promptly search for an infectious focus.

sepsis-unknown-focus-hospital-acquired.name: Sepsis / Septic shock with unknown focus (Hospital-acquired / Healthcare-associated)
sepsis-unknown-focus-hospital-acquired.presentation: Severe sepsis developing more than 48 hours post admission or recent invasive device/instrumentation
sepsis-unknown-focus-hospital-acquired.source_control: Prompt removal or exchange of suspicious central venous lines, urinary catheters, or foreign devices

primary_therapy.dose: Meropenem 1g IV q8h PLUS Vancomycin 15-20mg/kg IV q8-12h (loading dose 25-30mg/kg in critically ill)
primary_therapy.adjunct: Add Amikacin 15-20mg/kg IV once daily if multidrug-resistant Gram-negative organism suspected

alternative_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 15-20mg/kg IV q12h PLUS Amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h PLUS Ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h

sepsis-unknown-focus-hospital-acquired.comments: De-escalate to narrower spectrum agent as soon as culture and antimicrobial susceptibility results are available (at 48-72 hours).

surgical-prophylaxis-colorectal.name: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis - Colorectal surgery
surgical-prophylaxis-colorectal.presentation: Elective or emergency open or laparoscopic colorectal resection

primary_therapy.dose: Cefotaxime 1g IV PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV single dose at induction (within 60 minutes before skin incision)
primary_therapy.adjunct: Repeat dose if surgery exceeds 3-4 hours or blood loss more than 1500mL

primary_therapy.dose: Co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV single dose within 60 minutes before skin incision

alternative_therapy.dose: Gentamicin 5mg/kg IV PLUS Metronidazole 500mg IV single dose at induction

surgical-prophylaxis-colorectal.comments: Single pre-operative dose is sufficient in the vast majority of cases. Post-operative continuation of prophylactic antimicrobials beyond 24 hours is NOT recommended.

surgical-prophylaxis-orthopaedic-implant.name: Surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis - Orthopaedic arthroplasty and internal fixation
surgical-prophylaxis-orthopaedic-implant.presentation: Elective hip/knee joint arthroplasty or open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of fractures

primary_therapy.dose: Cefazolin 2g IV (3g if body weight more than 120kg) given 30-60 minutes before skin incision / tourniquet inflation
primary_therapy.adjunct: Re-dose Cefazolin 1g if procedure duration exceeds 4 hours

alternative_therapy.condition: Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity or known MRSA colonization
alternative_therapy.dose: Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV infusion started 60-120 minutes prior to surgical incision

surgical-prophylaxis-orthopaedic-implant.comments: Administer prior to inflation of pneumatic tourniquet to ensure adequate tissue concentration. Discontinue antimicrobial prophylaxis at skin closure or maximum within 24 hours post-operatively.

sp-cardiac-surgery-and-cardiology-proced.name: Cardiac surgery and cardiology procedures e.g. coronary artery bypass graft (CABG), valvular surgeries, repair of congenital anomalies, placement of implantable cardiac devices including ventricular assist devices and pacemakers

alternative_therapy.condition: Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity or in units with high prevalence of MRSA and for patients colonized with MRSA

sp-cardiac-surgery-and-cardiology-proced.comments: Vancomycin dose should not exceed more than 1.5g per dose in adults. Gentamicin can be added as a single dose when Gram negative pathogens are a concern.

sp-thoracic-surgeries.name: Thoracic surgeries e.g. insertion of prosthetic material, video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), mediastinoscopy, pneumonectomy/ lobectomy

alternative_therapy.condition: Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity or in units with high prevalence of MRSA and for patients colonized with MRSA

sp-thoracic-surgeries.comments: Vancomycin dose should not exceed more than 1.5g per dose in adults. Gentamicin can be added as a single dose when Gram negative pathogens are a concern.

sp-vascular-surgery.name: Vascular surgery e.g. reconstruction of abdominal aorta, aneurysm repair, thrombo-endarterectomy, vein bypass, procedures on the leg that involve a groin incision (except for varicose veins) or implantation of foreign material, lower extremity amputation for ischemia

alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin IV/ teicoplanin IV + gentamicin IV

sp-vascular-surgery.comments: Vancomycin dose should not exceed more than 1.5g per dose in adults. Metronidazole IV can be added for amputations of an ischaemic limb.

sp-ent-clean-contaminated.name: ENT surgery - prophylaxis is recommended for clean contaminated procedures that involve an invasion through oral, nasal, pharyngeal or oesophageal mucosa and stapedectomy
sp-ent-clean-contaminated.comments: Prophylaxis is not recommended for clean ear surgery (e.g. tympanostomy with tube placement, tympanoplasty), simple septorhinoplasty, endoscopic sinus surgery, clean head and neck surgeries (e.g. thyroidectomy, salivary gland excisions, parathyroidectomy) and tonsillectomy.

sp-ent-grommet-insertion.name: ENT surgery - grommet insertion
sp-ent-grommet-insertion.comments: Single topical dose is recommended after grommets insertion.

sp-endoscopic-peg-pej.name: Endoscopic procedures - percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG)/ percutaneous endoscopic jejunostomy (PEJ) placement
sp-endoscopic-peg-pej.comments: Contact microbiologist for prophylaxis in complicated endoscopic surgeries.

sp-endoscopic-eus-ercp.name: Endoscopic procedures - interventional endoscopic ultrasound guided (EUS) procedures (e.g. EUS-FNA of cystic lesion), endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP)
sp-endoscopic-eus-ercp.comments: Ciprofloxacin orally given within 60 to 90 minutes prior to procedure or IV beginning within 120 minutes prior to procedure (infusion given over 60 minutes). Contact microbiologist for prophylaxis in complicated endoscopic surgeries.

sp-hernia-repair-with-mesh.name: General surgery - hernia repair with mesh

sp-breast-surgeries.name: General surgery - breast surgeries (breast cancer surgery, reshaping procedures, breast surgery with implants)

alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin IV/ teicoplanin IV + gentamicin IV

sp-upper-gi-surgery.name: Gastro-intestinal surgery - upper GI surgery e.g. oesophageal/ gastro-duodenal procedures involving entry into lumen of gastrointestinal tract (bariatric, pancreatico-duodenectomy, gastrectomy, oesophagectomy, fundoplication), procedures without entry into GI tract (antireflux, highly selective vagotomy) for high-risk patients

alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin IV/ clindamycin IV + gentamicin IV

sp-upper-gi-surgery.comments: In complicated surgeries (e.g. gastric stasis, perforation, spillage at operation) antibiotics may be continued up to 48 hours.

sp-lower-gi-small-intestine-unobstructed.name: Lower GI surgery - small intestinal surgery (unobstructed)

sp-lower-gi-small-intestine-obstructed.name: Lower GI surgery - small intestinal surgery (obstructed)

sp-appendectomy-colorectal-surgery.name: Lower GI surgery - appendectomy, colorectal surgery

alternative_therapy.dose: clindamycin IV/ metronidazole IV + gentamicin IV

sp-appendectomy-colorectal-surgery.comments: Patients with complicated appendicitis (with infectious complications), should receive empirical therapy before surgery and therapy is tailored according to sensitivity results. Antibiotics may be continued for up to 48 hours in complicated surgeries and review the need after 48 hours.

sp-elective-lap-cholecystectomy-low-risk.name: Hepatobiliary - elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for biliary pain and low risk of infection (no current or previous acute cholecystitis / no common bile duct calculi / no immune suppression or no prosthetic implants)
sp-elective-lap-cholecystectomy-low-risk.comments: Antibiotic prophylaxis is not indicated. The biliary tract is usually sterile. Patients with bacteria in the bile at the time of surgery may be at higher risk of postoperative infection; however, some studies have found no association between the presence of bacteria in the bile and infection.

sp-elective-lap-cholecystectomy-with-ris.name: Hepatobiliary - elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy with risk of infection

alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin IV / clindamycin IV + gentamicin IV

sp-elective-lap-cholecystectomy-with-ris.comments: Patients with pre-existing infection in the hepato-biliary tract should receive empirical antimicrobials for the infection before surgery and targeted according to sensitivity results.

sp-open-hepatobiliary-procedures.name: Hepatobiliary - open procedures (cholecystectomy/ liver or pancreatic resection)

alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin IV / clindamycin IV + gentamicin IV

sp-open-hepatobiliary-procedures.comments: Patients with pre-existing infection in the hepato-biliary tract should receive empirical antimicrobials for the infection before surgery and targeted according to sensitivity results.

sp-complicated-open-hepatopancreatobilia.name: Hepatobiliary - complicated open hepatopancreatobiliary surgery (resections including Whipple / with biliary stent or drain)

alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin IV + ciprofloxacin IV + metronidazole IV

sp-complicated-open-hepatopancreatobilia.comments: Patients with pre-existing infection in the hepato-biliary tract should receive empirical antimicrobials for the infection before surgery and targeted according to sensitivity results.

sp-clean-head-and-neck-surgery.name: Head, neck and neurosurgeries - clean (e.g. thyroidectomy, lymph node biopsy, parotidectomy)
sp-clean-head-and-neck-surgery.comments: Antibiotic prophylaxis is not indicated. Prophylaxis is not indicated for clean head and neck surgeries.

sp-clean-head-and-neck-with-prosthesis.name: Head, neck and neurosurgeries - clean head and neck surgeries with prosthesis

alternative_therapy.condition: In units with high prevalence of MRSA and for patients colonized with MRSA

sp-clean-contaminated-head-and-neck.name: Head, neck and neurosurgeries - clean-contaminated head and neck surgeries

alternative_therapy.condition: In units with high prevalence of MRSA

sp-clean-contaminated-head-and-neck.comments: Duration of antibiotics for clean contaminated surgeries depends on the patient's condition.

sp-neurosurgery-craniotomy-csf-shunting.name: Neurosurgeries - elective craniotomy and cerebrospinal fluid shunting procedures

alternative_therapy.condition: In units with high prevalence of MRSA and for patients colonized with MRSA

sp-neurosurgery-craniotomy-csf-shunting.comments: For spinal surgeries with implants, the antibiotics may be continued for 24 hours.

sp-neurosurgery-intrathecal-pumps-spinal.name: Neurosurgeries - implantation of intrathecal pumps, spinal surgery with/without implants

alternative_therapy.condition: In units with high prevalence of MRSA and for patients colonized with MRSA

sp-neurosurgery-intrathecal-pumps-spinal.comments: For spinal surgeries with implants, the antibiotics may be continued for 24 hours.

sp-obstetric-gynaecological-minor-proced.name: Obstetric and gynaecological surgery - insertion of IUD, hysteroscopy, assisted delivery, miscarriage, diagnostic laparoscopy and sterilization (not laparoscopic entering uterine cavity/ vagina), dilatation and curettage
sp-obstetric-gynaecological-minor-proced.comments: Antibiotic prophylaxis is not indicated. Screening for Chlamydia trachomatis in high-risk population should be considered before IUD insertion and hysteroscopy.

sp-hysterosalpingography.name: Obstetric and gynaecological surgery - hysterosalpingography
sp-hysterosalpingography.comments: Antibiotic prophylaxis is not indicated. Patients should be screened and treated for Chlamydia trachomatis before uterine instrumentation procedures. Antibiotic prophylaxis (e.g. doxycycline) can be considered if screening is not done.

sp-caesarean-section.name: Obstetric and gynaecological surgery - caesarean section (elective/ emergency)
sp-caesarean-section.comments: Evidence favours giving prophylaxis before skin incision than giving after cord clamping for caesarean section.

sp-hysterectomy.name: Obstetric and gynaecological surgery - hysterectomy (abdominal/ laparoscopic/vaginal)

sp-ophthalmic-surgery.name: Ophthalmic surgery - cataract surgery, vitrectomy, keratoplasty, intraocular lens implantation, glaucoma procedures, strabotomy, retinal detachment repair, laser in situ keratomileusis, laser-assisted subepithelial keratectomy

primary_therapy.dose: Topical moxifloxacin or gatifloxacin eye drops or neomycin-polymyxin B-gramicidin eye drops or 5% betadine eye drops

sp-ophthalmic-surgery.comments: Aseptic procedures such as appropriate draping and pre-op assessment are better and effective methods for prevention of post-surgical eye infections. The addition of subconjunctival, intracameral or intravitreal cefuroxime or fourth generation fluoroquinolones at the end of the procedure is optional.

sp-oro-maxillofacial-surgeries.name: Oro maxillofacial surgeries e.g. orthognathic surgeries, temporomandibular joint surgery, surgical extractions of third molars, open reduction and internal fixation of compound mandibular fractures, major resections of tumors/ cysts, complex implants and intraoral bone grafting procedures
sp-oro-maxillofacial-surgeries.comments: Prophylactic antibiotic use is not routinely recommended for clean facial surgeries and tonsillectomy.

sp-orthopaedic-clean-hand-knee-foot.name: Orthopaedic surgery - clean operations involving hand, knee or foot and not involving implantation of foreign materials

sp-orthopaedic-implants-joint-replacemen.name: Orthopaedic surgery - total joint replacement/ internal fixation of closed fractures/hip fracture repair/spinal surgery/implantation of internal fixation devices (nails, screws, plates, wires), procedures involving other foreign material

alternative_therapy.condition: Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity or in units with high prevalence of MRSA and for patients colonized with MRSA
alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin IV/ teicoplanin IV + gentamicin IV

sp-orthopaedic-implants-joint-replacemen.comments: The prophylactic antimicrobial infusions should be completed 10 minutes prior to inflation of the proximal tourniquet. Gentamicin is added when Gram negatives are a concern and should be limited to a single dose. Flucloxacillin adult dose should be 2g IV.

sp-peritoneal-dialysis-catheter-placemen.name: Peritoneal dialysis catheter placement
sp-peritoneal-dialysis-catheter-placemen.comments: In settings with high prevalence of MRSA vancomycin is preferred.

sp-plastic-surgery.name: Plastic surgery - clean with risk factors or clean contaminated

sp-renal-heart-lung-transplant.name: Solid organ transplant surgery - renal transplant, heart transplant, lung transplant

alternative_therapy.condition: Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity or in units with high prevalence of MRSA and for patients colonized with MRSA

sp-renal-heart-lung-transplant.comments: Gentamicin should be considered in the possibility of Gram negative infection and should be limited to a single dose. Other antibiotics should be continued for <48 hours.

sp-pancreas-or-pancreas-kidney-transplan.name: Solid organ transplant surgery - pancreas or pancreas-kidney transplant

alternative_therapy.condition: Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity or in units with high prevalence of MRSA and for patients colonized with MRSA

sp-pancreas-or-pancreas-kidney-transplan.comments: Gentamicin should be considered in the possibility of Gram negative infection and should be limited to a single dose. Other antibiotics should be continued for <48 hours. IV fluconazole should be used as a single dose in patients with higher risk of fungal infection in patients undergoing pancreas or pancreas-kidney transplant. Antifungals should be used according to the individual risk given as a single dose.

sp-liver-transplant.name: Solid organ transplant surgery - liver transplant

primary_therapy.dose: cefotaxime IV / ceftriaxone IV + ampicillin IV

alternative_therapy.condition: Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity or in units with high prevalence of MRSA and for patients colonized with MRSA

sp-liver-transplant.comments: Gentamicin should be considered in the possibility of Gram negative infection and should be limited to a single dose. Other antibiotics should be continued for <48 hours. Antifungals should be used according to the individual risk given as a single dose.

sp-urology-low-risk-procedures.name: Urological surgeries/ procedures - flexible cystoscopy/ urodynamic studies/ catheterization, or catheter changes/ clean surgeries in low-risk patients (e.g. circumcision, orchidectomy, orchidopexy, varicocelectomy, inguino-scrotal surgery (non-prosthetic surgeries))
sp-urology-low-risk-procedures.comments: Antibiotic prophylaxis is not indicated. Prior to urological procedures/surgeries entering urinary tract, patients should be screened and treated for asymptomatic bacteriuria or UTI according to the antibiotic sensitivity. Antibiotic prophylaxis for patients with hip or knee prostheses is recommended during genitourinary surgeries/procedures which carry high risk of bacteraemia, within two years of prosthesis implant. Prophylaxis is not indicated in healthy people. However, prophylaxis is indicated in adults and children with strongly suspected or already proven urinary tract abnormalities when they undergo imaging procedures involving the urinary tract/ urodynamics/voiding cystourethrography (VCUG) and in children with urological malformations or a previous history of recurrent UTI before cystoscopy, ureteroscopy, and all other endoscopic procedures.

sp-lower-tract-instrumentation-turp-turb.name: Urological surgeries/ procedures - lower tract instrumentation with risk factors for infection (TURP, TURBT), rigid cystoscopy, ureteroscopy

sp-trus-prostate-biopsy.name: Urological surgeries/ procedures - trans-rectal ultrasound (TRUS) prostate biopsy

sp-clean-urologic-without-entry.name: Urological surgeries/ procedures - clean urologic procedures without entry into the urinary tract (e.g. nephrectomy and adrenalectomy)

sp-clean-urologic-with-entry.name: Urological surgeries/ procedures - clean urologic procedures with entry into the urinary tract (e.g. bladder reconstruction, nephroureterectomy and prostatectomy)

sp-clean-contaminated-urinary-tract.name: Urological surgeries/ procedures - clean-contaminated procedures of the urinary tract (often entering the gastrointestinal tract/vagina) (e.g. radical cystectomy with urinary diversion/ ileal conduit/ neobladder)

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin IV/ gentamicin IV + metronidazole IV/ clindamycin IV

sp-urinary-stone-surgery.name: Urological surgeries/ procedures - urinary stone surgery (e.g. shock wave lithotripsy (high risk procedures), percutaneous nephrolithotripsy, transurethral ureterolithotripsy)

alternative_therapy.dose: gentamicin IV / ciprofloxacin IV / co-trimoxazole PO

sp-urinary-stone-surgery.comments: For low-risk shock wave lithotripsy procedures, antibiotic prophylaxis is not indicated. High risk shock wave lithotripsy procedures include: the presence of bacteriuria, infected stone, endoscopic manipulation, repeated procedures, history of febrile urinary tract infection, stone diameter ≥2 cm, hydronephrosis etc.

post-splenectomy-antibiotic-prophylaxis.name: Post splenectomy antibiotic prophylaxis

primary_therapy.dose: PO. Adults and children over 5 years: 250mg q12h; Children 1-5 years: 125mg q12h; Children <1 year: 62.5mg q12h
PO. Adults: 250mg q24h; Children: 20mg/kg q24h (up to 250mg)

alternative_therapy.dose: PO. Adults and children over 2 years: 250mg q24h; Children 1 month-2 years: 10 mg/kg (up to 250mg) q24h

post-splenectomy-antibiotic-prophylaxis.comments: Antibiotic prophylaxis needs to be given irrespective of vaccinations. Duration in adults: at least for 2 years after splenectomy. Duration in children: at least up to the age of 5 years. Lifelong prophylaxis should be considered for the following categories: 1) Immunodeficient patients 2) History of severe sepsis 3) Patients who underwent splenectomy for a haematological disorder or malignancy that requires ongoing treatment

rheumatic-fever-prophylaxis.name: Rheumatic fever

primary_therapy.dose: IM. Adult and children >27kg: 900mg (1.2 MU) every 3-4 weeks; Children ≤27kg: 450mg (600,000 units) every 3-4 weeks

alternative_therapy.dose: PO. Weight >27 kg: 250 mg q24h; Weight ≤27 kg: 5 mg/kg (up to 250 mg) q24h
PO 250mg q12h for all ages (10 mg/kg q12h)

rheumatic-fever-prophylaxis.comments: Duration: If no rheumatic carditis: continue prophylaxis 5 years after the acute rheumatic fever or until age 21 years, whichever is longer. Carditis without residual valvular disease: continue prophylaxis for 10 years after the acute rheumatic fever or until age 21 years, whichever is longer. Carditis with residual valvular disease: continue prophylaxis for 10 years since the last episode or until age 40 years, whichever is longer. Lifelong prophylaxis may be needed.

infective-endocarditis-prophylaxis.name: Infective endocarditis
infective-endocarditis-prophylaxis.presentation: Prophylaxis is indicated for patients with risk conditions undergoing procedures mentioned in pages 194 and 195

primary_therapy.dose: IV or IM. Adults: 2g; Children: 50 mg/kg

alternative_therapy.dose: IV or IM. Adults: 1g; Children: 50 mg/kg

infective-endocarditis-prophylaxis.comments: Prophylaxis should be given as a single dose 30-60 minutes before the procedure.

meningitis-prophylaxis.name: Meningitis - significant exposures to invasive meningococcal infections or invasive Haemophilus influenzae type b infections (after exposure risk assessment)

primary_therapy.dose: PO single dose. Adults: 500mg; Children: Infants <1 year: 30mg/kg to a maximum 125mg; 1-<5 years: 125mg; ≥5-11 years: 250mg; ≥12 years: 500mg
PO q24h for 4 days. Adults: 600mg; Children: 1-<3 months: 10mg/kg; >3 months-11 years: 20mg/kg (max.600mg); ≥12-18 years: 600mg

alternative_therapy.dose: IM single dose. Adults: 250mg; Children: 1 month-11 years: 125mg; ≥12-18 years: 250mg
PO q12h for 2 days. Adults: 600mg; Children: Neonate-<1 year: 5mg/kg; 1-11 years: 10mg/kg (max.600mg); ≥12-18 years: 600mg
IM/IV q24h for 2 days. Adults and children older than 12 years: 1g; Children younger than 12 years: 50mg/kg (max.1g)

meningitis-prophylaxis.comments: Indications for prophylaxis - contact microbiologist. Pregnant Women: Single dose of ciprofloxacin 500mg PO/ ceftriaxone 250mg IM/ azithromycin 500mg PO.

cirrhosis-sbp-prophylaxis-primary-second.name: Cirrhosis - prevention of SBP: patients with low protein content in ascitic fluid and no prior history of SBP (primary prophylaxis), patients with a previous history of SBP (secondary prophylaxis)
cirrhosis-sbp-prophylaxis-primary-second.presentation: The antibiotic prophylaxis should strictly be restricted to patients at high risk of SBP: i) patients with acute bleeding ii) patients with low protein content in ascitic fluid and no prior history of SBP (primary prophylaxis) iii) patients with a previous history of SBP (secondary prophylaxis)

alternative_therapy.dose: PO 750mg once a week/ 500 mg q24h
PO 960mg q24h for 5 days per week

cirrhosis-sbp-prophylaxis-primary-second.comments: Duration needs to be decided by the attending physician

cirrhosis-sbp-prophylaxis-active-varicea.name: Cirrhosis - prevention of SBP: patients with active variceal bleeding
cirrhosis-sbp-prophylaxis-active-varicea.comments: Duration needs to be decided by the attending physician

cirrhosis-gi-bleeding-prior-to-endoscopy.name: Cirrhosis - patients with gastro-intestinal bleeding prior to endoscopy

primary_therapy.dose: PO 400mg 1 hour before procedure and then q12h for 1-2 days

alternative_therapy.condition: If oral therapy is not feasible
alternative_therapy.dose: IV 400mg at induction and then q12h for 1-2 days

recurrent-cellulitis-prophylaxis.name: Recurrent cellulitis
recurrent-cellulitis-prophylaxis.presentation: Considered in patients who have 2 or more attacks of cellulitis per year associated with lymphoedema

primary_therapy.dose: PO 250 mg (500mg if BMI >33 kg/m²) q12h

recurrent-cellulitis-prophylaxis.comments: No clinical consensus exists regarding effectiveness and duration. Following two years of successful prophylaxis, discontinuation should be considered.

child-neonatal-eos-suspected.name: Neonatal sepsis - early onset sepsis (EOS) <72 hours of age, suspected EOS
child-neonatal-eos-suspected.comments: Collect blood culture before giving the first dose of antibiotics. However, antibiotics should not be delayed if blood culture facilities are not readily available. Contact paediatrician/neonatologist immediately. IV ampicillin is preferred when there is a possibility of Listeria monocytogenes infection. Exclude CNS involvement by performing lumbar puncture (LP) as early as possible.

child-neonatal-eos-severe.name: Neonatal sepsis - severe EOS
child-neonatal-eos-severe.comments: Collect blood culture before giving the first dose of antibiotics. However, antibiotics should not be delayed if blood culture facilities are not readily available. Contact paediatrician/neonatologist immediately. IV ampicillin is preferred when there is a possibility of Listeria monocytogenes infection. Exclude CNS involvement by performing lumbar puncture (LP) as early as possible.

child-neonatal-los.name: Neonatal sepsis - late onset sepsis (LOS) >72 hours of age
child-neonatal-los.comments: MDRO risk factors include: low birth weight, prematurity, invasive procedures, IV lines in situ, antibiotic use and NICU stay. If risk factors for MRSA are present, add IV vancomycin.

child-neonatal-los-severe-mdro.name: Neonatal sepsis - severe LOS (risk of Multi Drug Resistant Organisms - MDRO)
child-neonatal-los-severe-mdro.comments: MDRO risk factors include: low birth weight, prematurity, invasive procedures, IV lines in situ, antibiotic use and NICU stay. If risk factors for MRSA are present, add IV vancomycin.

child-probable-nec.name: Probable necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC)
child-probable-nec.comments: Contact paediatrician immediately. Antifungal therapy with fluconazole should be considered for premature infants with a history of recent or prolonged antibiotic therapy or for infants with very low birth weight.

child-sepsis-unknown-focus-stable.name: Sepsis beyond neonatal period - unknown focus of sepsis in haemodynamically stable immunocompetent child
child-sepsis-unknown-focus-stable.comments: Collect blood and urine for culture. Contact paediatrician immediately. Consider adding IV vancomycin if suspecting MRSA (having long lines, undergoing haemodialysis, having prosthesis in situ etc.) Consider possible immunodeficiencies in children with unusual presentations / recurrent infections. Adding IV amikacin should be considered when suspecting Gram negative sepsis depending on the possible focus and when there is a possibility of healthcare associated infection. IV ciprofloxacin and IV amikacin can be used as alternatives to beta-lactams when there is a history of immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity.

child-sepsis-unknown-focus-unstable.name: Sepsis beyond neonatal period - unknown focus of sepsis in haemodynamically unstable immunocompetent child

primary_therapy.dose: cefotaxime IV/ ceftriaxone IV + gentamicin IV/ amikacin IV

child-sepsis-unknown-focus-unstable.comments: Collect blood and urine for culture. Contact paediatrician immediately. Consider adding IV vancomycin if suspecting MRSA. Adding IV amikacin should be considered when suspecting Gram negative sepsis depending on the possible focus and when there is a possibility of healthcare associated infection. IV ciprofloxacin and IV amikacin can be used as alternatives to beta-lactams when there is a history of immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity.

child-sepsis-unstable-immunocompromised.name: Sepsis beyond neonatal period - unknown focus of sepsis in haemodynamically unstable immunocompromised child including neutropenic child with evidence of sepsis
child-sepsis-unstable-immunocompromised.comments: Collect blood and urine for culture. Contact paediatrician immediately. Consider adding IV vancomycin if suspecting MRSA. Consider possible immunodeficiencies in children with unusual presentations / recurrent infections.

child-febrile-neutropenia-stable.name: Febrile neutropenia in haemodynamically stable child

child-meningitis-neonates.name: Central nervous system infections - meningitis in neonates
child-meningitis-neonates.comments: Perform blood and CSF cultures as early as possible. Refer BNF for Children for meningitis doses. Consider adding IV vancomycin if MRSA is suspected. The cephalosporin should be IV ceftazidime/ IV cefepime if Pseudomonas is suspected.

child-meningitis-beyond-neonatal.name: Central nervous system infections - meningitis beyond neonatal period

alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin IV + ciprofloxacin IV + metronidazole IV

child-meningitis-beyond-neonatal.comments: Perform blood and CSF cultures as early as possible. Refer BNF for Children for meningitis doses. Consider adding IV vancomycin if MRSA is suspected.

child-cns-shunt-infection-neurosurgery-t.name: Central nervous system infections - shunt infection, post-neurosurgery, head trauma or CSF leak
child-cns-shunt-infection-neurosurgery-t.comments: Perform blood and CSF cultures as early as possible. The cephalosporin should be IV ceftazidime/ IV cefepime if Pseudomonas is suspected.

child-encephalitis.name: Central nervous system infections - encephalitis
child-encephalitis.comments: Send CSF for viral studies including HSV PCR.

child-brain-abscess.name: Central nervous system infections - brain abscess

primary_therapy.dose: cefotaxime IV/ ceftriaxone IV + metronidazole IV

child-brain-abscess.comments: Perform blood and CSF cultures as early as possible. Consider adding IV vancomycin if MRSA is suspected.

child-endocarditis-native-or-late-prosth.name: Bacterial endocarditis - native valves/late prosthetic valve, after 1 year of surgery

primary_therapy.dose: benzylpenicillin IV/ ceftriaxone IV + gentamicin IV

child-endocarditis-native-or-late-prosth.comments: At least 3 blood cultures from different venipuncture sites should be obtained, with the first and last samples drawn at least 1 hour apart. Contact paediatric cardiologist and microbiologist.

child-endocarditis-early-prosthetic-or-n.name: Bacterial endocarditis - early prosthetic valve or nosocomial

primary_therapy.dose: vancomycin IV + gentamicin IV + cefepime IV/ ceftazidime IV

child-endocarditis-early-prosthetic-or-n.comments: At least 3 blood cultures from different venipuncture sites should be obtained, with the first and last samples drawn at least 1 hour apart. Contact paediatric cardiologist and microbiologist.

child-uti-neonates-and-1-3-months.name: Urinary tract infections - neonates suspected to have UTI, and UTI 1-3 months of age
child-uti-neonates-and-1-3-months.comments: Refer to the section on neonatal sepsis for the management of neonates suspected to have UTI. Collect urine sample for culture before starting antibiotics. Infants younger than 3 months with a possible UTI should be referred for specialist care immediately and the treatment should be with parenteral antibiotics.

child-afebrile-uti-3-months-to-3-years.name: Afebrile UTI/ lower UTI (bacteriuria without systemic symptoms or signs) - 3 months to 3 years of age
child-afebrile-uti-3-months-to-3-years.comments: Empirical therapy is not recommended unless the child has significant symptoms. Reassess 48 hours after initiating empirical therapy. Children <3 years should be given IV antibiotics initially if oral therapy is not tolerated or compliance is poor. Empiric therapy for recurrent UTI can be guided by previous ABST. Children on prophylactic antibiotics should not receive the same antibiotic for empirical therapy. Do not use nitrofurantoin if eGFR is <45 ml/min

child-afebrile-uti-3-years-or-above.name: Afebrile UTI/ lower UTI (bacteriuria without systemic symptoms or signs) - 3 years or above
child-afebrile-uti-3-years-or-above.comments: Empirical therapy is not recommended unless the child has significant symptoms. Reassess 48 hours after initiating empirical therapy. Empiric therapy for recurrent UTI can be guided by previous ABST. Children on prophylactic antibiotics should not receive the same antibiotic for empirical therapy. Do not use nitrofurantoin if eGFR is <45 ml/min

child-febrile-or-upper-uti.name: Febrile UTI/ Upper UTI ≥3 months of age (bacteriuria and fever ≥38°C or bacteriuria with loin pain/ tenderness)

alternative_therapy.dose: gentamicin IV/ amikacin IV/ ciprofloxacin PO/IV

child-febrile-or-upper-uti.comments: Start IV therapy and refer for specialist care if the child is 1. not tolerating oral therapy 2. ill or septic 3. having possible obstructive uropathy 4. immunosuppressed. The latter 3 groups need immediate specialist care.

child-septic-arthritis-osteomyelitis-und.name: Septic arthritis / Acute osteomyelitis - <3 months

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin IV + clindamycin IV/ vancomycin IV

child-septic-arthritis-osteomyelitis-und.comments: In all suspected acute septic arthritis/ osteomyelitis blood and synovial fluid aspirates and bone biopsies for culture should be obtained. Urgent surgical intervention reduces the risk of serious complications in septic arthritis but should not delay antibiotics. If community acquired MRSA is suspected, consider adding IV vancomycin or IV clindamycin. Total 3 weeks of IV antibiotics are indicated for neonates.

child-septic-arthritis-osteomyelitis-3-m.name: Septic arthritis / Acute osteomyelitis - 3 months to <5 years

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin IV + clindamycin IV/ vancomycin IV

child-septic-arthritis-osteomyelitis-3-m.comments: In all suspected acute septic arthritis/ osteomyelitis blood and synovial fluid aspirates and bone biopsies for culture should be obtained. Urgent surgical intervention reduces the risk of serious complications in septic arthritis but should not delay antibiotics. If community acquired MRSA is suspected, consider adding IV vancomycin or IV clindamycin.
