child-septic-arthritis-osteomyelitis-5-y.name: Septic arthritis / Acute osteomyelitis - 5 years and above
child-septic-arthritis-osteomyelitis-5-y.comments: In all suspected acute septic arthritis/ osteomyelitis blood and synovial fluid aspirates and bone biopsies for culture should be obtained. If community acquired MRSA is suspected, consider adding IV vancomycin or IV clindamycin.

child-acute-cough-with-urti.name: Respiratory tract infections - acute cough with upper respiratory tract infection
child-acute-cough-with-urti.comments: Antibiotics are not indicated. Most commonly due to viral aetiology. Review if symptoms are persistent or worsening.

child-acute-cough-high-risk-or-unwell.name: Respiratory tract infections - acute cough with high risk of complications or systemically unwell
child-acute-cough-high-risk-or-unwell.comments: High risk category involves children with comorbidities and younger children born prematurely.

child-cap-severe.name: Community acquired pneumonia - severe

primary_therapy.dose: co-amoxiclav IV/ cefuroxime IV/ ceftriaxone IV/ cefotaxime IV + clarithromycin PO

alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin IV/ teicoplanin IV + ciprofloxacin IV

child-cap-severe.comments: Blood cultures should be collected. Consider IV vancomycin if MRSA is suspected. Contact microbiologist if melioidosis is suspected based on clinical or epidemiological features.

child-hap-non-severe.name: Hospital acquired pneumonia - non-severe/ early onset and not at risk of harbouring MDRO
child-hap-non-severe.comments: Conditions with a high risk of harbouring MDRO include severe lung disease, immunosuppression, recent use of broad-spectrum antibiotics, prior colonization with MDRO, recent contact with health care settings etc.

child-hap-severe.name: Hospital acquired pneumonia - severe/ late onset/ symptoms of sepsis/ at risk of harbouring MDRO

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin IV + teicoplanin IV/ vancomycin IV

child-hap-severe.comments: Conditions with a high risk of harbouring MDRO include severe lung disease, immunosuppression, recent use of broad-spectrum antibiotics, prior colonization with MDRO, recent contact with health care settings etc.

child-vap-onset-under-5-days.name: Ventilator associated pneumonia - onset <5 days after intubation

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin IV + teicoplanin IV/ vancomycin IV

child-vap-onset-5-days-or-more.name: Ventilator associated pneumonia - onset ≥5 days after intubation

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin IV + teicoplanin IV/ vancomycin IV

child-probable-pertussis.name: Probable pertussis (cough for two or more weeks with one of the following - paroxysms of cough, inspiratory whoop, post-tussive emesis without another cause)

child-sore-throat-tonsillitis.name: Sore throat/ Tonsillitis - if bacterial infection is suspected
child-sore-throat-tonsillitis.comments: Most commonly due to viral aetiology. Antibiotics are indicated if systemically unwell/high risk of complications/pus on tonsils/ severely inflamed tonsils

child-scarlet-fever.name: Scarlet fever
child-scarlet-fever.comments: Scarlet fever is a bacterial illness that develops in children who have streptococcal sore-throat. Patients will have distinctive pink-red rash.

child-otitis-externa.name: Otitis externa
child-otitis-externa.presentation: Antibiotics are indicated if there is evidence of cellulitis/disease extending outside the ear canal/ systemic infection

primary_therapy.dose: flucloxacillin PO/ co-amoxiclav PO + ciprofloxacin ear drops

child-acute-otitis-media.name: Acute otitis media
child-acute-otitis-media.presentation: Antibiotics are indicated if <5 months of age/ systemically unwell/ <2 years of age with bilateral acute otitis media/ evidence of otorrhoea/ having cranio-facial malformations
child-acute-otitis-media.comments: Refer for specialist care if severe infection or evidence of complications are present.

child-epiglottitis-bacterial-tracheitis.name: Epiglottitis/bacterial tracheitis (laryngo-tracheo-bronchitis)
child-epiglottitis-bacterial-tracheitis.comments: Consider IV vancomycin if MRSA is suspected. Levofloxacin is a "Reserve Category" antibiotic (Annex 01).

child-cervical-lymphadenitis-parotitis.name: Acute bacterial cervical lymphadenitis/ Acute bacterial parotitis

alternative_therapy.dose: clarithromycin PO or clindamycin PO/ IV

child-cervical-lymphadenitis-parotitis.comments: Antibiotics are not indicated for otherwise well child with few systemic symptoms or generalized lymphadenopathy.

primary_therapy.dose: ceftriaxone IV/ cefotaxime IV + metronidazole IV + vancomycin IV

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin IV + metronidazole IV + vancomycin IV

child-orbital-cellulitis.name: Eye infections - orbital cellulitis
child-orbital-cellulitis.comments: Refer to an eye surgeon. Add IV vancomycin if MRSA is suspected.

child-ophthalmia-neonatorum.name: Ophthalmia neonatorum

primary_therapy.dose: cefotaxime IV single dose (immediately) + chloramphenicol eye drops
primary_therapy.adjunct: If C. trachomatis infection is suspected add azithromycin PO

child-ophthalmia-neonatorum.comments: Need urgent ophthalmology review. Send specimens (swabs) for chlamydia and gonococcus after discussing with the district clinics of NSACP. Investigate for maternal infection (refer to NSACP guideline) Consider HSV if vesicles are present and add IV aciclovir.

child-community-acquired-complicated-int.name: Community acquired complicated intra-abdominal infections - mild to moderate

primary_therapy.dose: cefotaxime IV/ ceftriaxone IV + metronidazole IV

child-community-acquired-complicated-int.comments: Source identification and control is vital.

child-community-acquired-complicated-int.name: Community acquired complicated intra-abdominal infections - severe/health care associated infections
child-community-acquired-complicated-int.comments: Source identification and control is vital.

child-watery-diarrhoea.name: Acute gastroenteritis - watery diarrhoea
child-watery-diarrhoea.comments: Antibiotics are not indicated. Most cases of acute gastroenteritis are caused by viruses and are self-limiting.

child-blood-and-mucus-diarrhoea-well.name: Acute gastroenteritis - blood and mucus diarrhoea, patient systemically well
child-blood-and-mucus-diarrhoea-well.comments: Antibiotic therapy is not usually indicated. The risk of haemolytic uraemic syndrome increases if antibiotics are given.

child-blood-and-mucus-diarrhoea-unwell.name: Acute gastroenteritis - blood and mucus diarrhoea, patient systemically unwell
child-blood-and-mucus-diarrhoea-unwell.comments: The risk of haemolytic uraemic syndrome increases if antibiotics are given. IV cefotaxime/ceftriaxone may be indicated in severe illness caused by Shigella spp.

child-cellulitis-mild.name: Skin and soft tissue infections - cellulitis, mild

child-cellulitis-moderate-to-severe.name: Skin and soft tissue infections - cellulitis, moderate to severe
child-cellulitis-moderate-to-severe.comments: If rapidly progressive add IV clindamycin. If risk factors for MRSA are present add IV vancomycin.

child-necrotizing-fasciitis.name: Skin and soft tissue infections - necrotizing fasciitis
child-necrotizing-fasciitis.comments: If risk factors for MRSA are present, add IV vancomycin. May consider IV meropenem in immunocompromised children.

child-impetigo.name: Skin and soft tissue infections - impetigo

primary_therapy.dose: Topical 2% ointment/cream on crusted areas 3 times a day
PO if widespread or large lesions

asymptomatic-bacteriuria-in-pregnancy.name: Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy
asymptomatic-bacteriuria-in-pregnancy.comments: Routine screening with urine culture is currently not practised. If asymptomatic bacteriuria is confirmed, treat for 4-7 days according to antibiotic sensitivity.

lower-uti-in-pregnancy.name: Lower UTI in pregnancy
lower-uti-in-pregnancy.comments: Contact microbiologist in immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity. Avoid nitrofurantoin in 3rd trimester and in women with an eGFR of <45ml/minute. Treat for 7days. Perform urine cultures before starting antibiotics.

pyelonephritis-in-pregnancy.name: Pyelonephritis in pregnancy
pyelonephritis-in-pregnancy.comments: Contact microbiologist in sepsis/ immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity. Perform blood and urine cultures before starting antibiotics. Switch to oral therapy following clinical response. Complete 7-10 days depending on severity and response.

septic-abortion.name: Septic abortion

primary_therapy.dose: co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV q8h + gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV q8h + gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h + clindamycin 600mg IV q6h
piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6-8h + clindamycin 600mg IV q6h
meropenem 1g IV q8h + clindamycin 600mg IV q6h

alternative_therapy.dose: ceftriaxone 1-2g IV q24h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
ceftriaxone 1-2g IV q24h + clindamycin 600mg IV q6h
ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h + clindamycin 600mg IV q6h

septic-abortion.comments: Antibiotics should be started promptly prior to evacuation of the products of conception and continued afterwards. Contact microbiologist if suspecting STI. Send blood for cultures. If risk factors for MRSA are present replace clindamycin with vancomycin and metronidazole.

preterm-prelabour-rupture-of-membranes.name: Preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) from 24+ weeks of gestation

primary_therapy.dose: 250mg PO q6h for 10 days or until the woman is in established labour (whichever is sooner)

preterm-prelabour-rupture-of-membranes.comments: Obtain a vaginal swab for culture during the speculum examination for diagnosing PPROM. Assess mother and fetus regularly to detect infection.

chorioamnionitis.name: Chorioamnionitis (Intra amniotic infection syndrome - IAIS)

primary_therapy.dose: ampicillin 2g IV q6h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: cefotaxime 1g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
clindamycin 600mg IV q6h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h

chorioamnionitis.comments: Send relevant specimens for culture including blood cultures. If risk factors for MRSA are present add vancomycin or in instances where clindamycin is used, replace clindamycin with vancomycin and metronidazole.

intrapartum-prophylaxis-group-b-streptoc.name: Intrapartum prophylaxis for group B streptococcal (GBS) infection
intrapartum-prophylaxis-group-b-streptoc.presentation: GBS carriage, GBS bacteriuria, previously GBS infected baby, maternal pyrexia in labour (≥38°C), rupture of membranes ≥18 hours

primary_therapy.dose: 3g (5 MU) IV loading dose followed by 1.2g (2 MU) IV q4h until delivery

alternative_therapy.dose: 2g IV loading dose followed by 1g IV q4h until delivery

intrapartum-prophylaxis-group-b-streptoc.comments: Intrapartum antibiotics are indicated in GBS carriage, GBS bacteriuria, previously GBS infected baby, maternal pyrexia in labour (≥38°C), rupture of membranes ≥18 hours.

alternative_therapy.dose: cefuroxime 500mg PO q12h + metronidazole 400mg PO q12h
ceftriaxone 1-2g IV q24h + metronidazole 400mg PO q12h

primary_therapy.dose: ampicillin 2g IV q6h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h + clindamycin 600mg IV q6h
ampicillin 2g IV q6h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: ceftriaxone 1-2g IV q24h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h + clindamycin 600mg IV q6h
gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h

postpartum-endometritis-critically-ill.name: Postpartum endometritis - if critically ill

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h + clindamycin 600-900mg IV q6h

postpartum-endometritis-critically-ill.comments: Contact microbiologist if suspecting STI. Prompt surgical interventions are required. If risk factors for MRSA are present, replace clindamycin with vancomycin and metronidazole.

episiotomy-infections-superficial.name: Episiotomy infections - superficial

primary_therapy.dose: cefuroxime 500mg PO q12h + metronidazole 400mg PO q8h

episiotomy-infections-superficial.comments: Contact microbiologist if suspecting STI. If risk factors for MRSA are present, replace clindamycin with vancomycin and metronidazole.

episiotomy-infections-deep-necrotizing-f.name: Episiotomy infections - deep infections/ necrotizing fasciitis/ myonecrosis

primary_therapy.dose: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6-8h + clindamycin 600-900mg IV q8h
ticarcillin-clavulanate 3.2g IV q8h + clindamycin 600-900mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: ceftazidime 1-2g IV q8h + clindamycin 600-900mg IV q8h
ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h + clindamycin 600-900mg IV q8h

episiotomy-infections-deep-necrotizing-f.comments: Contact microbiologist if suspecting STI. Prompt surgical interventions are required. If risk factors for MRSA are present, replace clindamycin with vancomycin and metronidazole.

influenza-in-pregnancy.name: Influenza in pregnancy
influenza-in-pregnancy.comments: Oseltamivir should be started within 48 hours of onset of symptoms in a suspected or confirmed influenza infection during pregnancy at any trimester. But it is still recommended to start antiviral therapy even after 48 hours in late presentations. Send specimens for viral studies before starting antivirals if facilities are available.

chickenpox-in-pregnancy.name: Chickenpox

primary_therapy.dose: 800mg PO 5 times per day for 7 days

chickenpox-in-pregnancy.comments: Therapy should ideally be given within the first 24 hours of onset of rash. Intravenous aciclovir should be given under specialist care to all pregnant women with severe chickenpox. Neonates of mothers who have chickenpox 7 days prior to or 7 days after delivery should be given a single dose of varicella zoster immunoglobulin. Contact virologist/microbiologist.

post-exposure-prophylaxis-chickenpox-or-.name: Post exposure prophylaxis following a significant exposure to a case of chicken pox or shingles

primary_therapy.dose: <20 weeks of gestation: single dose of varicella zoster immunoglobulin (VZIG)
>20 weeks of gestation: single dose of varicella zoster immunoglobulin or aciclovir 800mg PO q6h from day 7 to 14 after exposure

alternative_therapy.dose: If VZIG is not available, aciclovir 800mg PO q6h from day 7 to 14 after exposure can be considered

post-exposure-prophylaxis-chickenpox-or-.comments: Contact virologist. When contact occurs with chickenpox or shingles, a careful history must be taken to confirm the significance of exposure and the susceptibility of the patient. If exposure is significant, immunity for VZV should be established. If patient is not having evidence of immunity, refer to VOG as soon as possible after the first exposure (up to 10days) for administering VZIG or considering prophylactic aciclovir.

vulvovaginal-candidiasis-uncomplicated.name: Vulvovaginal candidiasis - uncomplicated infection (first or single isolated infection)

primary_therapy.dose: pessary 500mg intravaginally at night as a single dose

alternative_therapy.dose: pessary 100-200mg intravaginally at night for 7 consecutive nights
vaginal cream (2%) 5g intravaginally at night for 7 consecutive nights

vulvovaginal-candidiasis-uncomplicated.comments: Oral therapies must be avoided in pregnancy. Topical imidazoles are a safe and effective alternative. Refer to VOG for the management of non-responding/complicated/recurrent infections.

febrile-neutropenia-low-risk-adults.system: Febrile Neutropenia/ Infections in HSCT Recipients
febrile-neutropenia-low-risk-adults.name: Febrile neutropenia in low-risk adults
febrile-neutropenia-low-risk-adults.presentation: Outpatient status at the time of development of fever, anticipated short duration of severe neutropenia (≤100 cells/mm³ for <7 days), good performance status, no comorbidities, no hepatic insufficiency, no renal insufficiency, MASCC risk index score 21 or above

primary_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 500mg PO q12h + co-amoxiclav 625 mg PO q8h
ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 500mg PO q12h + clindamycin 300-450mg PO q6h
ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + clindamycin 600mg IV q8h

febrile-neutropenia-low-risk-adults.comments: If patients are discharged on oral antibiotics, ensure careful observation and access to medical care 24/7. Review in 3-5 days to evaluate response and culture results. Possibility of ciprofloxacin resistance should be considered if there is a recent exposure to fluoroquinolones. Contact microbiologist.

febrile-neutropenia-high-risk.system: Febrile Neutropenia/ Infections in HSCT Recipients
febrile-neutropenia-high-risk.name: Febrile neutropenia in high-risk patients

primary_therapy.adjunct: +/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h/ amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h
+/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h/ amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h
+/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h/ amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h

febrile-neutropenia-high-risk.comments: Combination therapy could be considered if antibiotic resistance is suspected (due to recent antibiotic exposure or institutional resistance pattern) or proven with previous culture results. Contact microbiologist if fever persists beyond 96 hours of antibacterial therapy or if there is clinical deterioration.

febrile-neutropenia-mrsa-risk.system: Febrile Neutropenia/ Infections in HSCT Recipients
febrile-neutropenia-mrsa-risk.name: Febrile neutropenia in high-risk patients - patients colonized with MRSA/ clinical evidence of a vascular catheter related infection/ skin and soft tissue infection/ pneumonia/ in a unit with a high incidence of MRSA infection

primary_therapy.dose: 15mg/kg IV 12h in addition to above antibiotics

alternative_therapy.dose: 400mg IV q12h for 3 doses followed by 400mg q24h in addition to above antibiotics

febrile-neutropenia-mrsa-risk.comments: Teicoplanin is preferred in patients with renal impairment.

febrile-neutropenia-candida-risk-factors.system: Febrile Neutropenia/ Infections in HSCT Recipients
febrile-neutropenia-candida-risk-factors.name: Febrile neutropenia - patients with risk factors for candida infections
febrile-neutropenia-candida-risk-factors.comments: Risk factors for candida infections: patients who have persistent or recurrent fever after 4-7 days of broad-spectrum antibiotics or overall duration of neutropenia for >7 days and no identified source of fever

febrile-neutropenia-mould-risk-factors.system: Febrile Neutropenia/ Infections in HSCT Recipients
febrile-neutropenia-mould-risk-factors.name: Febrile neutropenia - patients with risk factors for mould infections
febrile-neutropenia-mould-risk-factors.presentation: neutropenia lasting >10 days, allogenic HSCT recipients, treatment with high dose corticosteroids

primary_therapy.dose: 6mg/kg IV q12h 2 doses followed by 4mg/kg IV q12h
400mg PO q12h followed by 200mg PO q12 h

febrile-neutropenia-mould-risk-factors.comments: If the patient has renal insufficiency, liposomal amphotericin B 3-5mg/kg IV once daily may be started after discussing with microbiologist. Read the product leaflet carefully before using both products of amphotericin B. Amphotericin B and voriconazole are "Reserve Category" antifungals (Annex 01).

febrile-neutropenia-critically-ill-or-un.system: Febrile Neutropenia/ Infections in HSCT Recipients
febrile-neutropenia-critically-ill-or-un.name: Febrile neutropenia in critically ill or haemodynamically unstable patients

primary_therapy.dose: meropenem 1-2g IV q8h + vancomycin 1g IV q12h
imipenem 1g IV q8h or 500mg IV q6h + vancomycin 1g IV q12h

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h for 3 doses followed by 400mg IV q24h + amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h/ gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h

febrile-neutropenia-critically-ill-or-un.comments: If typhlitis is suspected add metronidazole.

immunodeficiency-asymptomatic-bacteriuri.name: Asymptomatic bacteriuria/candiduria
immunodeficiency-asymptomatic-bacteriuri.comments: Empirical treatment is not indicated. In renal transplant recipients, repeat culture with appropriate technique to rule out contamination. During the first 3 months of post-transplant, consider treatment for 5-7 days; beyond 3 months, post-transplant, avoid treatment unless associated with a rise in serum creatinine. Treatment is indicated if awaiting instrumentation. Await culture susceptibility results and select a narrow-spectrum antibiotic according to antibiotic sensitivity pattern.

immunodeficiency-symptomatic-urinary-tra.name: Symptomatic urinary tract infection
immunodeficiency-symptomatic-urinary-tra.comments: Similar to non-immunocompromised patients. Refer chapter 21.

immunodeficiency-community-or-hospital-a.name: Community acquired pneumonia/Hospital acquired pneumonia (HAP should be suspected if the patient has been hospitalised during the preceding 3 months)
immunodeficiency-community-or-hospital-a.comments: Similar to non-immunocompromised patients. Refer chapter 18. Anti-pseudomonal and anti-MRSA cover should be provided if risk factors for these infections are present. Empirical antifungal chemotherapy is only indicated when clinical and radiological presentation strongly suggests a fungal origin. If not responding to initial empirical treatment, uncommon bacterial, fungal and parasitic infections should be suspected. Contact microbiologist.

immunodeficiency-cns-infections.name: Central nervous system infections e.g. acute meningitis, chronic meningitis, meningoencephalitis, brain abscesses or focal neurological deficits

primary_therapy.dose: ampicillin 2g IV q4h + cefotaxime 2g IV q6h/ ceftriaxone 2g IV q12h + vancomycin 30-45 mg/kg IV q8-12h + aciclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: chloramphenicol 1-1.5g IV q6h + vancomycin 30-45mg/kg IV q8-12h + cotrimoxazole 5 mg/kg (trimethoprim component) PO q5-8 h + aciclovir 10mg/kg IV q8h

immunodeficiency-cns-infections.comments: Dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg IV started before or with the first dose of antibiotic. Then continue 6 hourly for 2-4 days. Add metronidazole when brain abscess is suspected. If not responding to initial antimicrobials, mycobacterial, fungal and parasitic infections should be suspected. Contact microbiologist.

immunodeficiency-post-liver-transplant-i.name: Post liver transplant intra-abdominal infections

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

immunodeficiency-post-liver-transplant-i.comments: Consider antifungal in the early post-transplant period if risk factors are present. If CMV colitis is suspected IV ganciclovir should be considered. Contact microbiologist.

immunodeficiency-moderate-to-severe-gast.name: Moderate to severe gastroenteritis (≥6 stools per day or bloody stool)
immunodeficiency-moderate-to-severe-gast.comments: Blood cultures are indicated when fever is present.

immunodeficiency-chronic-diarrhoea.name: Chronic diarrhoea (>14 days) without severe clinical signs
immunodeficiency-chronic-diarrhoea.comments: Empiric antibiotics therapy is not indicated.

immunodeficiency-clostridioides-difficil.name: Clostridioides difficile-associated infections (CDI)
immunodeficiency-clostridioides-difficil.comments: Refer chapter 13. Immunocompromised patients are at increased risk for CDI. For people living with HIV, antiretroviral therapy is strongly recommended to reduce the incidence of recurrent opportunistic infections.

oropharyngeal-candidiasis-mild.name: Oropharyngeal candidiasis - mild

primary_therapy.dose: suspension 500,000 units (5ml) swish and swallow q6h for 7-14 days

oropharyngeal-candidiasis-mild.comments: For people living with HIV, antiretroviral therapy is strongly recommended to reduce the incidence of recurrent opportunistic infections.

oropharyngeal-candidiasis-moderate-to-se.name: Oropharyngeal candidiasis - moderate to severe

alternative_therapy.dose: solution 200 mg PO q24h for up to 28 days

oropharyngeal-candidiasis-moderate-to-se.comments: For people living with HIV, antiretroviral therapy is strongly recommended to reduce the incidence of recurrent opportunistic infections.

candida-oesophagitis.name: Candida oesophagitis

primary_therapy.dose: 200-400 mg PO (3-6 mg/kg) q24h for 14-21 days

alternative_therapy.condition: For patients who cannot tolerate oral therapy
For patients who cannot tolerate oral therapy

candida-oesophagitis.comments: For people living with HIV, antiretroviral therapy is strongly recommended to reduce the incidence of recurrent opportunistic infections. Voriconazole is a "Reserve Category" antifungal (Annex 01).

immunodeficiency-bacterial-skin-and-soft.name: Bacterial skin and soft tissue infections

mucocutaneous-herpes-simplex-virus-infec.name: Mucocutaneous Herpes Simplex Virus infection

primary_therapy.dose: 400mg PO 5 times per day for 7 days

mucocutaneous-herpes-simplex-virus-infec.comments: Continue treatment until lesions have completely healed.

varicella-zoster-virus-infection-chicken.name: Varicella zoster virus infection (chicken pox)

primary_therapy.dose: 800mg PO 5 times per day for 7 days
primary_therapy.adjunct: Patients with complications: aciclovir 10mg/kg IV infusion q8h for 5 days

varicella-zoster-virus-infection-chicken.comments: Continue treatment until lesions have completely healed.

herpes-zoster-shingles.name: Herpes Zoster (shingles)

primary_therapy.dose: 800mg PO 5 times per day for 7-10 days
primary_therapy.adjunct: in severe cases aciclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h for 7-14 days

herpes-zoster-shingles.comments: IV aciclovir can be considered with following risk factors: advanced age >60y, corticosteroid dose >7.5 mg to 10 mg prednisone-equivalent dose (PEQ), history of recurrent shingles, presence of ocular/neurologic or disseminated disease. Continue treatment until lesions have completely healed.

penetrating-cranio-cerebral-injury.name: Head and neck trauma - penetrating cranio-cerebral injury

primary_therapy.dose: cefuroxime 1.5g IV stat followed by 750mg IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin 1g IV q12h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

depressed-or-basal-skull-fracture.name: Head and neck trauma - depressed skull fractures, simple basal skull fracture with or without CSF leak
depressed-or-basal-skull-fracture.comments: Antimicrobial prophylaxis is not required. If there is cranial CSF leak, consider pneumococcal vaccine. If the patient develops signs of meningitis, refer to empirical antibiotics for meningitis associated with neuro-trauma (chapter 12).

penetrating-abdominal-trauma.name: Penetrating abdominal trauma

primary_therapy.dose: cefuroxime 1.5g IV stat followed by 750mg IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

penetrating-abdominal-trauma.comments: Reassess after 24 hours regarding continuation of antibiotics. Discontinue prophylactic antibiotics after 24 hours if there is no acute hollow viscous injury. If there are ruptured viscera, consider treatment than prophylaxis.

penetrating-chest-injury-requiring-chest.name: Thoracic trauma - penetrating chest injury requiring chest drain placement

primary_therapy.dose: cefuroxime 1.5g IV stat followed by 750mg IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

penetrating-chest-injury-requiring-chest.comments: Reassess after 24 hours to decide on continuation. Prophylaxis is not indicated for blunt chest trauma.

open-limb-fractures-type-i-and-ii.name: Open limb fractures - Type I and II
open-limb-fractures-type-i-and-ii.presentation: Type I: open fracture with a skin wound < 1 cm in length and clean. Type II: open fracture with a laceration > 1 cm in length without extensive soft tissue damage, flaps, or avulsions
open-limb-fractures-type-i-and-ii.comments: Metronidazole IV should be added in the presence of faecal or potential clostridial contamination (e.g. farm related injuries). Review the requirement of continuation of antibiotics beyond 24hours.

open-limb-fractures-type-iii.name: Open limb fractures - Type III
open-limb-fractures-type-iii.presentation: Type III: open segmental fracture with > 10 cm wound with extensive soft tissue injury or a traumatic amputation (special categories in Type III include gunshot fractures and open fractures caused by farm injuries). Type IIIA: adequate soft tissue coverage. Type IIIB: significant soft tissue loss with exposed bone that requires soft tissue transfer to achieve coverage. Type IIIC: associated vascular injury that requires repair for limb preservation

primary_therapy.dose: cefuroxime 1.5g IV stat followed by 750mg IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: clindamycin 600mg IV q6-8h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h

open-limb-fractures-type-iii.comments: Metronidazole IV should be added in the presence of faecal or potential clostridial contamination (e.g. farm related injuries). Review the requirement of continuation of antibiotics beyond 24hours. In type III fractures, antibiotics should be continued for 72 hours after injury or not more than 24 hours after soft tissue coverage has been achieved.

bites-human-and-animal.name: Bites (human and animal)

alternative_therapy.dose: metronidazole 400mg PO q8h + doxycycline 200mg PO (loading dose) followed by 100mg PO q24h for 2-7 days

bites-human-and-animal.comments: Infected bites: 5 days. Prophylaxis: only 3 days. Risk of tetanus/rabies and blood-borne infection to be considered.

burns-no-evidence-of-infection.name: Burns - with no evidence of infection
burns-no-evidence-of-infection.comments: Available evidence does not support systemic antibiotic therapy for clinically non-infected burn wounds.

burns-with-evidence-of-infection.name: Burns - with evidence of infection
burns-with-evidence-of-infection.comments: Select antibiotics to cover Pseudomonas spp. and Enterobacterales, based on culture and severity of infection.

burns-with-evidence-of-infection-critica.name: Burns - with evidence of infection and critically ill

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + vancomycin 1g IV q12h

burns-with-evidence-of-infection-critica.comments: Select antibiotics to cover Pseudomonas spp. and Enterobacterales, based on culture and severity of infection.

brucellosis-non-focal-adults-and-childre.name: Brucellosis - non-focal, adults and children >8yrs

primary_therapy.dose: doxycycline 100mg PO q12h for 6 weeks + gentamicin 5mg/kg/day IV or IM q24h for 7-10 days

alternative_therapy.dose: doxycycline 100mg PO q12h for 6 weeks + rifampicin 15mg/kg PO (600-900mg) divided in q12h/q8h for 6 weeks

brucellosis-non-focal-adults-and-childre.comments: Send samples for serological diagnosis (blood and CSF) and culture for Brucella spp. (blood and bone marrow). Consult microbiologist for suspected/ confirmed cases or those presenting with focal/complicated infections including endocarditis and neuro-brucellosis who need prolonged treatment and alternative therapy. Doxycycline to be considered in <8 years only if no other options available. Refer to BNF for gentamicin dosage in paediatric population.

brucellosis-non-focal-children-under-8-y.name: Brucellosis - non-focal, children <8yrs

primary_therapy.dose: co-trimoxazole 5 mg/kg PO (TMP component) q12h for 6 weeks + rifampicin 15-20mg/kg/day PO divided in q12h/q8h for 6wks

brucellosis-non-focal-children-under-8-y.comments: Send samples for serological diagnosis (blood and CSF) and culture for Brucella spp. (blood and bone marrow). Consult microbiologist for suspected/ confirmed cases or those presenting with focal/complicated infections including endocarditis and neuro-brucellosis who need prolonged treatment and alternative therapy. Doxycycline to be considered in <8 years only if no other options available. Refer to BNF for gentamicin dosage in paediatric population.

enteric-fever-mild-moderate-uncomplicate.name: Enteric fever - mild-moderate / uncomplicated (GI manifestations only)

primary_therapy.dose: 400mg IV q12h or 500mg PO q12h for 7-14 days

alternative_therapy.dose: 1g PO single dose followed by 500mg PO q24h for 5-7days
500mg PO q6h for 14 days/ 12.5-25mg/kg IV q6h for 14 days

enteric-fever-mild-moderate-uncomplicate.comments: Obtain blood samples for culture. Tailor treatment according to latest local susceptibility data. Clinical improvement precedes defervescence. In cases of continuing fever, contact microbiologist and exclude endocarditis and other complications. Empirical treatment should only be based on local or individual susceptibility patterns for these options.

enteric-fever-severe-or-complicated.name: Enteric fever - severe or complicated cases
enteric-fever-severe-or-complicated.comments: Obtain blood samples for culture. Tailor treatment according to latest local susceptibility data. Clinical improvement precedes defervescence. In cases of continuing fever, contact microbiologist and exclude endocarditis and other complications. Empirical treatment should only be based on local or individual susceptibility patterns for these options.

enteric-fever-eradication-of-chronic-car.name: Enteric fever - eradication of chronic carriage

primary_therapy.dose: 500mg PO q12h for 28 days depending on susceptibility of the isolate

leptospirosis-mild-illness.name: Leptospirosis - mild illness

alternative_therapy.dose: 1g PO loading dose on day 1 followed by 500mg PO q24h for 2 more days in mild disease

leptospirosis-mild-illness.comments: Pre-exposure prophylaxis: Doxycycline 200mg PO once weekly. Start 1 to 2 days before exposure and continue throughout the period of the exposure. Currently, there is no recommended pre-exposure prophylaxis that is safe for pregnant and lactating women. Contact microbiologist for treatment options in immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity.

leptospirosis-moderate-severe-disease.name: Leptospirosis - moderate-severe disease
leptospirosis-moderate-severe-disease.comments: Pre-exposure prophylaxis: Doxycycline 200mg PO once weekly. Start 1 to 2 days before exposure and continue throughout the period of the exposure. Currently, there is no recommended pre-exposure prophylaxis that is safe for pregnant and lactating women. Contact microbiologist for treatment options in immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity.

melioidosis-intensive-phase-adults-singl.name: Melioidosis - intensive phase, adults, single focus mild to moderate infection
melioidosis-intensive-phase-adults-singl.comments: Intensive phase/induction stage should be followed by eradication stage. The duration and dose of intensive phase may vary according to severity and site from 2 to 8 weeks. Contact microbiologist in immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity.

melioidosis-intensive-phase-adults-sever.name: Melioidosis - intensive phase, adults, severe infection
melioidosis-intensive-phase-adults-sever.comments: Intensive phase/induction stage should be followed by eradication stage. The duration and dose of intensive phase may vary according to severity and site from 2 to 8 weeks. Contact microbiologist in immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity.

melioidosis-intensive-phase-adults-cns.name: Melioidosis - intensive phase, adults, CNS infection
melioidosis-intensive-phase-adults-cns.comments: Intensive phase/induction stage should be followed by eradication stage. The duration and dose of intensive phase may vary according to severity and site from 2 to 8 weeks. Contact microbiologist in immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity.

melioidosis-intensive-phase-children-sin.name: Melioidosis - intensive phase, children, single focus mild to moderate infection

alternative_therapy.dose: for non-CNS infections: <1 week, >1.5 kg: 25 mg/kg IV q12h; 1-4 weeks, >1.5 kg: 25 mg/kg IV q8h; 4 weeks-3 months, >1.5 kg: 25 mg/kg IV q6h; >3 months: 15-25 mg/kg IV q6h (not to exceed 2 g/day); >12 years: 10-15 mg/kg IV q6h

melioidosis-intensive-phase-children-sin.comments: Intensive phase/induction stage should be followed by eradication stage. The duration and dose of intensive phase may vary according to severity and site from 2 to 8 weeks. Contact microbiologist in immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity.

melioidosis-intensive-phase-children-cns.name: Melioidosis - intensive phase, children, CNS infection/severe infection

alternative_therapy.dose: for non-CNS infections: <1 week, >1.5 kg: 25 mg/kg IV q12h; 1-4 weeks, >1.5 kg: 25 mg/kg IV q8h; 4 weeks-3 months, >1.5 kg: 25 mg/kg IV q6h; >3 months: 15-25 mg/kg IV q6h (not to exceed 2 g/day); >12 years: 10-15 mg/kg IV q6h

melioidosis-intensive-phase-children-cns.comments: Intensive phase/induction stage should be followed by eradication stage. The duration and dose of intensive phase may vary according to severity and site from 2 to 8 weeks. Contact microbiologist in immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity.

melioidosis-adjunct-therapy-adults.name: Melioidosis - adjunct therapy, adults

primary_therapy.dose: co-trimoxazole <40kg: 10+50 mg/kg/day PO in two divided doses; 40-60kg: 240+1200mg PO q12h; >60kg: 320+1600mg PO q12h + folic acid 5mg PO q24h

melioidosis-adjunct-therapy-adults.comments: Oral co-trimoxazole is added during intensive phase therapy in cutaneous melioidosis, osteomyelitis or septic arthritis, central nervous system infection, deep seated collections, or infections with poor response to treatment.

melioidosis-adjunct-therapy-children.name: Melioidosis - adjunct therapy, children

primary_therapy.dose: co-trimoxazole 6+30 mg/kg up to 240+1200 mg PO q12h + folic acid. For <4 years: 0.3 mg PO q24h. For >4 years: 0.4 mg PO q24h

melioidosis-adjunct-therapy-children.comments: Oral co-trimoxazole is added during intensive phase therapy in cutaneous melioidosis, osteomyelitis or septic arthritis, central nervous system infection, deep seated collections, or infections with poor response to treatment.

melioidosis-eradication-phase-adults.name: Melioidosis - eradication phase, adults

primary_therapy.dose: co-trimoxazole >60kg: 320/1600mg PO q12h; 40-60kg: 240/1200mg PO q12h; <40 kg: 160 mg/800mg PO q12h + folic acid 5mg PO q24h

melioidosis-eradication-phase-adults.comments: The duration and dose of eradication phase may vary from 3-6 months according to severity and site.

melioidosis-eradication-phase-children.name: Melioidosis - eradication phase, children

primary_therapy.dose: co-trimoxazole 6+30 mg/kg up to 240+1200 mg PO q12h + folic acid. For <4 years: 0.3 mg PO q24h. For >4 years: 0.4 mg PO q24h

melioidosis-eradication-phase-children.comments: The duration and dose of eradication phase may vary from 3-6 months according to severity and site.

rickettsial-infections-adult.name: Rickettsial infections - adult
rickettsial-infections-adult.presentation: Scrub typhus, spotted fever group rickettsioses, typhus fever and other miscellaneous infections such as Q fever and ehrlichiosis

primary_therapy.dose: 200mg PO/IV loading dose on day 1 followed by 100mg PO/IV q12h for 5-7 days (10-14 days in severe disease)

alternative_therapy.dose: 500mg IV q6h or 50 mg/kg PO per day in four divided doses (maximum dose 4g/d) for 7-10 days

rickettsial-infections-adult.comments: Azithromycin is recommended for pregnant women and patients with doxycycline allergy. Doxycycline treatment should result in prompt defervescence. Persistent fever > 48 hours should raise the need to consider alternative diagnosis. Treatment decisions for Rickettsial pathogens should never be delayed while awaiting laboratory confirmation as this can lead to severe disease and long-term sequelae or death.

rickettsial-infections-children.name: Rickettsial infections - children
rickettsial-infections-children.presentation: Scrub typhus, spotted fever group rickettsioses, typhus fever and other miscellaneous infections such as Q fever and ehrlichiosis
rickettsial-infections-children.comments: Refer to BNF for Children for doses.

tetanus.name: Tetanus
tetanus.source_control: If wound is identified, debridement is essential

primary_therapy.dose: tetanus immunoglobulin (TIG) 500IU IM + metronidazole 500mg IV q6h or 400mg PO q8h for 7-10 days
primary_therapy.adjunct: Part of TIG dose can be infiltrated around the wound if identified

alternative_therapy.dose: intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) 200-400mg/kg can be given + benzylpenicillin 2-4MU IV q4-6h for 7-10 days
intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) 200-400mg/kg can be given + doxycycline 200mg PO loading dose on day 1 followed by 100mg PO q12h for 7-10 days

tetanus.comments: TIG or IVIG should be given as soon as the diagnosis of tetanus is considered. IV or intrathecal preparations of TIG can be considered if available. If wound is identified, debridement is essential. Vaccination with tetanus toxoid before discharge is required as patients with tetanus will not develop immunity following infection.

complicated-cystitis.name: Complicated cystitis - cystitis in patients with anatomical and functional anomalies, cystitis with underlying disease which increase the risk of more serious outcome or treatment failure, cystitis in men
complicated-cystitis.presentation: Cystitis in patients with anatomical and functional anomalies, cystitis with underlying disease which increase the risk of more serious outcome or treatment failure, cystitis in men

primary_therapy.dose: 50mg PO q6h/ 100mg PO q12h (sustained release capsules)

complicated-cystitis.comments: Previous antibiotic therapy, previous episodes of UTI and susceptibility patterns should be considered when selecting antibiotics. Do not use nitrofurantoin if CrCl<45 ml/min. Avoid multiple antibiotics. Duration of therapy: 7 days. If the patient cannot tolerate oral antibiotics, consider IV preparations. Recurrent UTIs could be due to re-infections or relapses. Treatment should be guided by previous culture and ABST.

acute-prostatitis.name: Acute prostatitis
acute-prostatitis.comments: For mild cases with prompt responses 14 days of antibiotic is recommended. For delayed response or severe cases longer duration of therapy is needed. If there is a risk of STI refer to guidelines issued by NSACP. If there is associated sepsis, consider intravenous antibiotics.

acute-uncomplicated-pyelonephritis-outpa.name: Pyelonephritis - acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis in non-pregnant women (absence of structural or functional anomalies of the urinary tract), out-patient
acute-uncomplicated-pyelonephritis-outpa.comments: Patients who don't have clinical evidence of sepsis and are able to take oral medication, can be managed as outpatient. Urine culture and susceptibility tests should always be performed. Blood culture should be done in patients with sepsis. Duration of treatment: 7-14 days according to the antibiotic used. Contact microbiologist.

acute-uncomplicated-pyelonephritis-inpat.name: Pyelonephritis - acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis in non-pregnant women (absence of structural or functional anomalies of the urinary tract), in-patient
acute-uncomplicated-pyelonephritis-inpat.comments: Urine culture and susceptibility tests should always be performed. Blood culture should be done in patients with sepsis. Review intravenous antibiotics in 48 hours and consider stepping down to oral antibiotics where possible depending on the clinical improvement and sensitivity pattern. A combination of antibiotics may be considered in sepsis or if there are concerns about antibiotic resistance. Duration of treatment: 7-14 days according to the antibiotic used. Contact microbiologist.

complicated-pyelonephritis.name: Complicated pyelonephritis
complicated-pyelonephritis.presentation: pyelonephritis in patients with anatomical and functional anomalies in the urinary tract, pyelonephritis in patients with underlying disease which increases the risk of more serious outcome or treatment failure, pyelonephritis in men

primary_therapy.dose: co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV q8h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h / amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)
ceftriaxone 1-2 g IV q24h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h / amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)
cefotaxime 1g IV q8h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h / amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)

alternative_therapy.adjunct: +/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h / amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)
+/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h / amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)
+/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h / amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h/ amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h

complicated-pyelonephritis.comments: Contact microbiologist for advice on choice and duration of antibiotic therapy in complicated pyelonephritis. Review aminoglycoside therapy at 48 hours.

pyelonephritis-with-sepsis-septic-shock-.name: Uncomplicated or complicated pyelonephritis with sepsis/ septic shock/ emphysematous pyelonephritis

primary_therapy.adjunct: +/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h / amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)
+/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h / amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)
+/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h / amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)

pyelonephritis-with-sepsis-septic-shock-.comments: Contact microbiologist for advice on choice and duration of antibiotic therapy. Consider surgical opinion.

catheterized-patient-asymptomatic-bacter.name: Catheterized patient - asymptomatic bacteriuria
catheterized-patient-asymptomatic-bacter.comments: Screening for and treatment of catheter associated asymptomatic bacteriuria is not recommended except in pregnant women, patients who undergo urologic procedures or early post kidney transplant period. Antimicrobial prophylaxis should not be routinely used.

cauti-cystitis-no-upper-uti.name: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections - cystitis in men and non-pregnant women without evidence of upper UTI

primary_therapy.dose: 50mg PO q6h or 100mg PO q12h (sustained release capsules)

cauti-cystitis-no-upper-uti.comments: Urinary catheter should be removed or replaced. A urine specimen for culture should be obtained from a new catheter or mid-stream sample if catheter is removed, prior to initiating antimicrobial therapy. Do not use nitrofurantoin if CrCl<45 ml/min. Duration: 7 days if responds promptly after change of catheter and 10-14 days is recommended for those with delayed response or pyelonephritis regardless of whether the patient remains catheterized or not. Contact microbiologist.

cauti-upper-uti-without-sepsis.name: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections - upper UTI without sepsis in men and non-pregnant women

primary_therapy.adjunct: +/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h / amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)

cauti-upper-uti-with-sepsis-or-septic-sh.name: Catheter-associated urinary tract infections - upper UTI with sepsis or septic shock

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h (for 48 hours)

erysipelas-localized-infection.name: Erysipelas - localized infection
erysipelas-localized-infection.comments: Continue antibiotic therapy for 5 days. Extension of therapy is considered up to 10 days if there is lack of symptom resolution at 5 days.

erysipelas-with-systemic-infection.name: Erysipelas - if signs of systemic infection present
erysipelas-with-systemic-infection.comments: Continue antibiotic therapy for 5 days. Extension of therapy is considered up to 10 days if there is lack of symptom resolution at 5 days.

cellulitis-mild-outpatient.name: Cellulitis - mild (outpatient therapy)
cellulitis-mild-outpatient.comments: Continue antibiotic therapy for 5 days. Extension of therapy is considered up to 10 days if there is lack of symptom resolution at 5 days.

cellulitis-moderate-inpatient.name: Cellulitis - moderate (inpatient therapy)
cellulitis-moderate-inpatient.comments: In patients at risk for Gram negative infections or severe forms (neutropenic and immunocompromised patients) who do not respond to first-line therapy or patients with sepsis or septic shock, contact microbiologist. Send a blood culture before starting antibiotics. Duration: 14 days. With good clinical response IV therapy can be converted to oral therapy.

cellulitis-severe-inpatient.name: Cellulitis - severe (inpatient therapy)
cellulitis-severe-inpatient.comments: In patients at risk for Gram negative infections or severe forms (neutropenic and immunocompromised patients) who do not respond to first-line therapy or patients with sepsis or septic shock, contact microbiologist. Send a blood culture before starting antibiotics. Duration: 14 days. With good clinical response IV therapy can be converted to oral therapy.

purulent-cellulitis-with-furuncles-outpa.name: Purulent cellulitis with furuncles (outpatient therapy)
purulent-cellulitis-with-furuncles-outpa.source_control: Incision & drainage should be combined with antibiotic treatment

alternative_therapy.dose: 200mg PO (loading dose) followed by 100mg PO q12h

purulent-cellulitis-with-furuncles-outpa.comments: Incision & drainage should be combined with antibiotic treatment. In patients at risk for Gram negative infections or severe forms (neutropenic and immunocompromised patients) who do not respond to first-line therapy or patients with sepsis or septic shock, contact microbiologist.

purulent-cellulitis-with-carbuncles-or-a.name: Purulent cellulitis with carbuncles or abscesses (inpatient therapy)
purulent-cellulitis-with-carbuncles-or-a.source_control: Incision & drainage should be combined with antibiotic treatment
purulent-cellulitis-with-carbuncles-or-a.comments: Incision & drainage should be combined with antibiotic treatment. In patients at risk for Gram negative infections or severe forms (neutropenic and immunocompromised patients) who do not respond to first-line therapy or patients with sepsis or septic shock, contact microbiologist.

cutaneous-abscesses-furuncles-carbuncles.name: Cutaneous abscesses, furuncles, carbuncles

primary_therapy.adjunct: For large lesions >5cm/ undrainable areas/ multiple lesions/ high risk patient for severe infection
For large lesions >5cm/ undrainable areas/ multiple lesions/ high risk patient for severe infection

cutaneous-abscesses-furuncles-carbuncles.comments: For small lesions <5cm, I & D would be sufficient. Antibiotic treatment is not indicated. I & D and send pus for culture and ABST. If no response after 2-3 days review for complications and consider IV therapy. If the MRSA risk is high, consider adding vancomycin/ teicoplanin. Contact microbiologist.

diabetic-foot-ulcer-mild-infection.name: Diabetic foot ulcer - mild infection

alternative_therapy.dose: clindamycin 300-450mg PO q6-8h + ciprofloxacin 500mg PO q12h

diabetic-foot-ulcer-mild-infection.comments: I & D and send pus for culture and ABST. If no response after 2-3 days review for complications and consider IV therapy. If the MRSA risk is high, consider adding vancomycin/ teicoplanin. Contact microbiologist. Antibiotic therapy is not recommended for ulcers without signs of inflammation. Use rotational antiseptics.

diabetic-foot-ulcer-severe-infection.name: Diabetic foot ulcer - severe infection

primary_therapy.adjunct: +/- vancomycin 1g IV q12h/ teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h for three doses followed by 400mg IV q24h
+/- vancomycin 1g IV q12h/ teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h for three doses followed by 400mg IV q24h

diabetic-foot-ulcer-severe-infection.comments: Exclude osteomyelitis. Contact microbiologist. Vancomycin/teicoplanin should be added if suspecting MRSA or if not responding within 48 hours.

impetigo.name: Impetigo - bullous/non-bullous

primary_therapy.adjunct: +/- flucloxacillin 500mg PO q6h / cephalexin 500mg PO q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: 200mg PO (loading dose) followed by 100mg PO q12h

impetigo.comments: Crusts need to be removed with soap and water or saline before local application. Oral antibiotics are recommended for patients with numerous lesions or in outbreaks. Duration 7 days.

mastitis-mild.name: Mastitis - mild (symptoms <24 hours)
mastitis-mild.presentation: If symptoms are not resolving within 12 to 24 hours with physiological methods, consider antibiotics
mastitis-mild.comments: Breast feeding can be continued or milk from the infected breast can be expressed manually or by a pump. Percutaneous aspiration / I&D if there is an abscess and pus should be sent for culture and sensitivity. Switch to oral therapy when symptoms resolve.

mastitis-moderate-severe.name: Mastitis - moderate-severe (symptoms >24 hours/ fever/ unwell/ breast abscess)

alternative_therapy.condition: Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity/ high risk of MRSA
Immediate beta-lactam hypersensitivity/ high risk of MRSA
alternative_therapy.dose: 400mg IV q12h for three doses then 400mg IV q24h

acute-paronychia.name: Paronychia (acute)
acute-paronychia.presentation: If soft tissue swelling is present without fluctuance, the infection may resolve with only warm soaks 3-4 times daily
acute-paronychia.comments: I & D if there is an abscess. Send pus for culture.

surgical-site-infection-mild.name: Surgical site infections - mild
surgical-site-infection-mild.comments: Systemic antibiotics are not necessary. Manage with antiseptics.

surgical-site-infection-mild-to-moderate.name: Surgical site infections - mild to moderate infections with surrounding cellulitis, non-GI tract surgery
surgical-site-infection-mild-to-moderate.comments: Send pus for culture prior to antibiotic therapy. Antibiotic choice in surgical site infections may differ according to the organism profile and antibiogram of surgical site infections of the hospital. Contact microbiologist.

surgical-site-infection-severe-non-gi.comments: Send pus/tissue specimens for culture prior to antibiotic therapy. Vancomycin/teicoplanin should be added if suspecting MRSA. surgical-site-infection-severe-gi.name: Surgical site infections - severe infections with systemic symptoms, GI tract surgery

alternative_therapy.dose: gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h + ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

surgical-site-infection-severe-gi.comments: Send pus/tissue specimens for culture prior to antibiotic therapy. Vancomycin/teicoplanin should be added if suspecting MRSA. Antibiotic choice in surgical site infections may differ according to the organism profile and antibiogram of surgical site infections of the hospital. Contact microbiologist.

community-acquired-sepsis-and-septic-sho.name: Community acquired sepsis and septic shock

primary_therapy.dose: ceftriaxone 2g IV q24h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h
cefotaxime 1g IV q8h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h

primary_therapy.adjunct: Meropenem should be restricted for instances where 3rd generation cephalosporin use cannot safely be recommended

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + clindamycin 600-900mg IV q6h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h

community-acquired-sepsis-and-septic-sho.comments: Contact microbiologist for continuation of gentamicin/amikacin after 48 hours or for alternative therapy. Add vancomycin/teicoplanin if MRSA is suspected or in a known colonizer. Antifungals are considered in patients with risk factors for invasive candidiasis, e.g. immunosuppressed status (neutropenia, chemotherapy, transplant, chronic liver dysfunction), invasive vascular devices, total parenteral nutrition, recent abdominal surgery, high APACHE (Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation) score, prolonged antibiotic exposure and hospitalization, candida colonization at multiple sites.

healthcare-associated-sepsis-and-septic-.name: Healthcare associated sepsis and septic shock

primary_therapy.dose: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6-8h + amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h
primary_therapy.adjunct: If MRSA is suspected or in a known colonizer: add teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h for 3 doses followed by 400mg IV q24h or vancomycin 1g IV q12h

primary_therapy.dose: meropenem 1g IV q8h + amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h
primary_therapy.adjunct: If MRSA is suspected or in a known colonizer: add teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h for 3 doses followed by 400mg IV q24h or vancomycin 1g IV q12h

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h
alternative_therapy.adjunct: If MRSA is suspected or in a known colonizer: add teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h for 3 doses followed by 400mg IV q24h or vancomycin 1g IV q12h

healthcare-associated-sepsis-and-septic-.comments: However individual patient factors should be assessed even among the group of patients mentioned in page 111 when starting antifungals. Contact mycologist/ microbiologist for opinion on empirical antifungals.

post-splenectomy-sepsis.name: Post-splenectomy sepsis
post-splenectomy-sepsis.comments: Patients should be investigated for malaria and treated accordingly if there is a history of recent visit to an endemic country. In patients with immediate beta-lactam allergy contact microbiologist.

acute-bronchitis.name: Acute bronchitis
acute-bronchitis.presentation: Antibiotics might be considered in a severe attack on initial presentation, persistent symptoms for 5-7 days with no evidence of resolution, patients with known cardiopulmonary disease, presence of abnormal lung signs, rising WBC and inflammatory markers

alternative_therapy.dose: 200mg PO (first dose) followed by 100mg PO q24h. Duration: 5 days

acute-bronchitis.comments: Antibiotics are usually not recommended as most are of viral origin. Avoid doxycycline in pregnancy and children. Fluroquinolones should be avoided. Caution: Ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin and moxifloxacin can mask / promote resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and atypical mycobacterial infections. Exclude pulmonary TB if cough persists. Erythromycin is recommended in pregnancy.

suspected-pertussis.name: Persistent paroxysmal cough >14 days - consider pertussis (inspiratory whoop, post tussive vomiting)

primary_therapy.dose: 500mg PO on day one followed by 250mg PO q24h for 5 days

suspected-pertussis.comments: Per nasal swabs / nasopharyngeal swabs/ aspirates should be collected and sent to Medical Research Institute for culture/ PCR in suspected cases of pertussis. Contact microbiologist for collection and transport of specimens.

copd-exacerbation-mild-no-pseudomonas-ri.name: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) - patients without risk factors for Pseudomonas infection: mild exacerbations
copd-exacerbation-mild-no-pseudomonas-ri.presentation: Mild exacerbations without risk factors for Pseudomonas infection

alternative_therapy.dose: 200mg PO (first dose) followed by 100mg PO q24h

copd-exacerbation-mild-no-pseudomonas-ri.comments: For mild exacerbations antibiotics may not be indicated as up to 50% are of viral origin. Antibiotics are indicated if at least 2 out of following 3 symptoms are present: 1. Increased dyspnoea 2. Increased sputum volume/ viscosity 3. Increased sputum purulence

copd-exacerbation-moderate-to-severe.name: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) - moderate to severe exacerbations (consider IV antibiotics if unable to take oral)
copd-exacerbation-moderate-to-severe.comments: Take nasopharyngeal/ throat swabs in viral transport medium for PCR/Ag detection. Contact microbiologist. Risk factors for Pseudomonas infection: 1. Chronic colonization or prior infection with Pseudomonas (particularly within the past 12 months) 2. Very severe COPD (FEV1<30% predicted) 3. Bronchiectasis on chest imaging 4. Broad spectrum antibiotics used within the past 3 months 5. Chronic systemic glucocorticoid use. These patients should ideally be managed in a specialized unit under a respiratory physician's supervision.

copd-exacerbation-pseudomonas-risk-facto.name: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) - patients with risk factors for Pseudomonas infection
copd-exacerbation-pseudomonas-risk-facto.comments: Risk factors for Pseudomonas infection: 1. Chronic colonization or prior infection with Pseudomonas (particularly within the past 12 months) 2. Very severe COPD (FEV1<30% predicted) 3. Bronchiectasis on chest imaging 4. Broad spectrum antibiotics used within the past 3 months 5. Chronic systemic glucocorticoid use. Take nasopharyngeal/ throat swabs in viral transport medium for PCR/Ag detection. Contact microbiologist. These patients should ideally be managed in a specialized unit under a respiratory physician's supervision.

acute-infective-exacerbation-of-bronchie.name: Acute infective exacerbation of bronchiectasis
acute-infective-exacerbation-of-bronchie.presentation: Clinical symptoms: change in character and severity of cough, or change in volume, purulence and viscosity of sputum, increasing breathlessness from baseline, fatigue/ malaise, haemoptysis

alternative_therapy.dose: 200mg PO (first dose) followed by 100mg PO q24h. Duration: 7-10 days

acute-infective-exacerbation-of-bronchie.comments: Caution: Ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin and moxifloxacin (quinolones) can mask / promote resistance of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and atypical mycobacterial infections. Send respiratory specimens for Mycobacterial diagnostics if TB or atypical mycobacteria is suspected. Anti-viral therapy is recommended for patients with clinical / laboratory evidence of Influenza infection. Contact microbiologist.

bronchiectasis-exacerbation-pseudomonas.name: Acute infective exacerbation of bronchiectasis - previous microbiologically confirmed or suspected infection with Pseudomonas spp.
bronchiectasis-exacerbation-pseudomonas.comments: Alternative therapy: discuss with microbiologist. For severe infections / patients with sepsis discuss with microbiologist / respiratory physician. Ertapenem is not effective for Pseudomonas spp.

empyema.name: Empyema

primary_therapy.dose: ceftriaxone 1-2g IV q24h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
cefotaxime 1g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + clindamycin 300-450mg PO q6-8h/600mg IV q8h

empyema.comments: Pus should be drained and sent for culture and ABST. Exclude Mycobacterium tuberculosis in sub-acute / chronic infections. Discuss with microbiologist for the duration of therapy. Piperacillin-tazobactam / meropenem may be started in patients with severe infection / poor response after discussing with the microbiologist/ respiratory physician.

alternative_therapy.dose: 400mg IV q12h for 3 doses followed by 400mg IV q24h

lung-abscess-systemically-well.name: Lung abscess - systemically well

primary_therapy.dose: amoxicillin 1g PO q8h + metronidazole 400mg PO q8h

lung-abscess-systemically-well.comments: If guided aspiration / drainage is possible, pus should be sent for culture and ABST. If features of sepsis are present, blood culture should be sent. If IV antibiotics are given, consider oral switch when sufficient clinical improvement is achieved. Contact microbiologist / respiratory physician for poorly responding infections, infections with suspected MDR organisms and for duration of treatment. Exclude Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.

lung-abscess-systemically-unwell.name: Lung abscess - systemically unwell

primary_therapy.dose: ceftriaxone 1-2 g IV q24h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
cefotaxime 1-2 g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: clindamycin 600mg IV q8h + ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h

lung-abscess-systemically-unwell.comments: If guided aspiration / drainage is possible, pus should be sent for culture and ABST. If features of sepsis are present, blood culture should be sent. If IV antibiotics are given, consider oral switch when sufficient clinical improvement is achieved. Contact microbiologist / respiratory physician for poorly responding infections, infections with suspected MDR organisms and for duration of treatment. Exclude Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.

lung-abscess-mrsa-suspected.name: Lung abscess - if MRSA is suspected

alternative_therapy.dose: 400mg IV q12h for 3 doses followed by 400mg IV q24h

lung-abscess-mrsa-suspected.comments: If guided aspiration / drainage is possible, pus should be sent for culture and ABST. Contact microbiologist / respiratory physician for poorly responding infections, infections with suspected MDR organisms and for duration of treatment. Exclude Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.

cap-mild-out-patient-no-comorbidities.name: Pneumonia community acquired - mild (CURB 65=0-1), out-patient, no comorbidities
cap-mild-out-patient-no-comorbidities.presentation: CURB 65 score can be used as a severity indicator. 1 point is allocated for each of: confusion (new onset), urea >7mmol/l (20mg/dl), respiratory rate >30/min, BP (systolic <90 or diastolic <60mmHg), age ≥65 years

alternative_therapy.dose: 500mg PO q6h (for use in pregnancy). Duration: 5 days
200mg PO (first dose) followed by 100mg PO q24h. Duration: 5 days

cap-mild-out-patient-no-comorbidities.comments: CURB 65 score ≥ 1 needs hospital admission. CURB 65 score 4-5 may need ICU care (Outpatient settings - where urea is not available CRB 65 may be used.) Other factors to consider in hospitalization: co-morbidities: poorly controlled DM, COPD, CRF, underlying malignancies etc. The decision to hospitalize a patient will ultimately depend on the judgment of the clinician. If antimicrobials were used within previous 3 months or in immediate beta-lactam allergy, contact microbiologist.

cap-mild-out-patient-with-comorbidities.name: Pneumonia community acquired - mild (CURB 65=0-1), out-patient, with comorbidities

primary_therapy.dose: co-amoxiclav 625mg PO q8h + clarithromycin 500mg PO q12h for a minimum duration of 5 days
cefuroxime 500mg PO q12h + clarithromycin 500mg PO q12h for a minimum duration of 5 days

cap-moderate.name: Pneumonia community acquired - moderate (CURB 65=2)

primary_therapy.dose: co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV q8h + clarithromycin 500mg PO q12h
cefuroxime 1.5g IV q8h + clarithromycin 500mg PO q12h

cap-moderate.comments: Levofloxacin is a "Reserve Category" antibiotic (Annex 01). Erythromycin is the preferred macrolide during pregnancy.

cap-severe.name: Pneumonia community acquired - severe (CURB 65=3-5)

primary_therapy.dose: cefotaxime 1-2 g IV q8h + clarithromycin 500mg IV/PO q12h
ceftriaxone 1-2g IV q24h + clarithromycin 500mg IV/PO q12h

cap-severe.comments: Levofloxacin is a "Reserve Category" antibiotic (Annex 01). Contact microbiologist if patient presents with sepsis, haemoptysis, multilobar infiltrates, and leucopenia. Specific combination therapy is recommended for PVL (Panton-Valentine leukocidin) producing CA-MRSA pneumonia.

cap-suspected-ca-mrsa.name: Pneumonia community acquired - suspected community acquired MRSA (CA-MRSA) pneumonia

alternative_therapy.dose: 400mg IV q12h for 3 doses then 400mg IV q24h

cap-suspected-ca-mrsa.comments: Contact microbiologist if patient presents with sepsis, haemoptysis, multilobar infiltrates, and leucopenia. Specific combination therapy is recommended for PVL (Panton-Valentine leukocidin) producing CA-MRSA pneumonia.

cap-pseudomonas-risk-factors.name: Pneumonia community acquired - with risk factors for Pseudomonas (cystic fibrosis, COPD, bronchiectasis)

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + gentamicin 5-7mg/kg IV q24h

cap-pseudomonas-risk-factors.comments: Risk factors for Pseudomonas infection: chronic colonization or prior infection with Pseudomonas (particularly within the past 12 months), very severe COPD (FEV1<30% predicted), bronchiectasis on chest imaging, broad spectrum antibiotics used within past 3 months, chronic systemic glucocorticoid use.

suspected-viral-pneumonia.name: Suspected viral pneumonia
suspected-viral-pneumonia.comments: Effective only in pneumonia due to influenza virus. Send specimens for viral studies before starting antivirals.

hap-vap-early-onset-no-mdr-risk.name: Hospital acquired pneumonia (HAP) or ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) - early onset (3-5 days after admission/ intubation) and no risk factors for multi-drug resistant organisms
hap-vap-early-onset-no-mdr-risk.presentation: Early onset: 3-5 days after admission/ intubation and no risk factors for multi-drug resistant organisms

primary_therapy.dose: ceftriaxone 2g IV q24h + clarithromycin 500mg PO/IV q12h
cefotaxime 1g IV q8h + clarithromycin 500mg PO/IV q12h

hap-vap-early-onset-no-mdr-risk.comments: Levofloxacin is a "Reserve Category" antibiotic (Annex 01). Risk factors for multi-drug resistant organisms: recent hospitalization, recent use of broad-spectrum antibiotics during preceding 90 days, haemodialysis, critical illness, presence of comorbidities (such as severe lung disease or immunosuppression), colonization with multidrug-resistant bacteria.

hap-vap-early-with-mdr-risk-or-late-onse.name: Early onset HAP/VAP with risk factors for MDR organisms or late onset HAP/VAP (>5 days after admission/ intubation)

primary_therapy.adjunct: +/- ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h/ amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h/ gentamicin 5-7mg/kg IV q24h
+/- ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h/ amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h/ gentamicin 5-7mg/kg IV q24h
+/- ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h/ amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h/ gentamicin 5-7mg/kg IV q24h

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h
ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + gentamicin 5-7mg/kg IV q24h

hap-vap-early-with-mdr-risk-or-late-onse.comments: For risk factors refer comment on page 107. Therapy should be guided by local antibiotic sensitivity data. Contact microbiologist. In severe infections and in obese patients, ciprofloxacin IV 400mg q8h can be given.

hap-vap-mrsa-suspected.name: HAP/VAP - if MRSA is suspected

alternative_therapy.dose: 400mg IV q12h for 3 doses followed by 400mg IV q24h

hap-vap-mrsa-suspected.comments: Therapy should be guided by local antibiotic sensitivity data. Contact microbiologist.

acute-suppurative-sialadenitis-parotitis.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
acute-suppurative-sialadenitis-parotitis.name: Acute suppurative sialadenitis/ suppurative parotitis

primary_therapy.dose: flucloxacillin 2g IV q6h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

acute-suppurative-sialadenitis-parotitis.comments: If high risk of MRSA or immunocompromised, contact microbiologist. Selection of PO/IV route should be done according to clinical condition at the time of starting empirical antibiotics. Minimum of 7 days therapy is recommended.

juvenile-recurrent-parotitis.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
juvenile-recurrent-parotitis.name: Juvenile recurrent parotitis
juvenile-recurrent-parotitis.comments: Refer BNF for children for paediatric doses. Selection of PO/IV route should be done according to clinical condition at the time of starting empirical antibiotics. Minimum of 7 days therapy is recommended.

cervico-facial-actinomycosis.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
cervico-facial-actinomycosis.name: Cervico-facial actinomycosis

primary_therapy.dose: benzylpenicillin 3-4MU IV q6h followed by phenoxymethylpenicillin 500mg-1g PO q6h

alternative_therapy.dose: 600mg IV q8h followed by 450mg PO q6h
200mg PO (loading dose) followed by 100mg PO q24h

cervico-facial-actinomycosis.comments: 2-6 weeks of parenteral therapy followed by oral therapy for a total duration of 6 - 12 months for serious infections and bulky disease, whereas a shorter duration for less extensive disease. Contact microbiologist.

dentoalveolar-infections.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
dentoalveolar-infections.name: Dentoalveolar infections (tooth abscess/ inflamed wisdom tooth area / root canal infection)
dentoalveolar-infections.presentation: Fever>100°F, malaise, lymphadenopathy, trismus, increased swelling, cellulitis, osteomyelitis, persistent infection
dentoalveolar-infections.source_control: Surgical drainage and removal of necrotic tissue is essential

primary_therapy.dose: amoxicillin 500mg PO q8h + metronidazole 400mg PO q8h for 3-5 days

dentoalveolar-infections.comments: Surgical drainage and removal of necrotic tissue is essential. Local treatment may be adequate in mild cases. Conditions not requiring adjunctive antibiotics: 1. Pain without signs and symptoms of infection 2. Symptomatic irreversible pulpitis 3. Acute peri-radicular periodontitis 4. Teeth with necrotic pulps and a radiolucency 5. Teeth with a sinus tract (chronic peri-radicular abscess) 6. Localized fluctuant swellings

ludwigs-angina-immunocompetent.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
ludwigs-angina-immunocompetent.name: Ludwig's angina - immunocompetent

primary_therapy.dose: benzylpenicillin 3MU IV q6h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

ludwigs-angina-immunocompetent.comments: Potentially life threatening. Manage the airway. Intravenous antibiotics to be given for a minimum period of 48 hours or until patient responds adequately. Then switch to oral therapy. Culture and antibiotic sensitivity are advised in parapharyngeal space infections. If high risk of MRSA or immunocompromised contact microbiologist.

ludwigs-angina-immunocompromised.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
ludwigs-angina-immunocompromised.name: Ludwig's angina - immunocompromised

parapharyngeal-space-infection-peritonsi.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
parapharyngeal-space-infection-peritonsi.name: Parapharyngeal space infection/peritonsillar abscess

periodontal-disease-gingivitis.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
periodontal-disease-gingivitis.name: Periodontal disease - gingivitis
periodontal-disease-gingivitis.comments: Chlorhexidine gluconate may be incompatible with some ingredients in toothpaste; leave an interval of at least 30 minutes between using mouthwash and toothpaste. Debridement is important. No indication for antibiotics.

periodontal-disease-necrotizing.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
periodontal-disease-necrotizing.name: Periodontal disease - necrotizing periodontal disease

alternative_therapy.dose: clindamycin 300-450mg PO q6-8h + metronidazole 400mg PO q8h

periodontal-disease-necrotizing.comments: Intravenous antibiotics may be required in severe infections. Duration of treatment is usually 7 days. Intravenous antibiotics are usually not indicated. Drainage and removal of the cause is important in all forms.

periodontitis-abscesses-of-the-periodont.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
periodontitis-abscesses-of-the-periodont.name: Periodontitis/ abscesses of the periodontium

alternative_therapy.dose: 200mg PO (loading dose) followed by 100mg PO q24h

periodontitis-abscesses-of-the-periodont.comments: Drainage and removal of the cause is important in all forms.

chronic-periodontitis.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
chronic-periodontitis.name: Chronic periodontitis
chronic-periodontitis.comments: Chronic periodontal disease should be managed by controlling bacterial plaque with hygiene measures and debridement of pocket root surfaces. Systemic antimicrobial use will be ineffective in microbial elimination within plaque biofilm.

aggressive-periodontitis.system: Oral Cavity and Associated Structure Infections
aggressive-periodontitis.name: Aggressive periodontitis

uncomplicated-cholecystitis.comments: When early surgical treatment (within 7-10 days) is offered, post-operative antibiotics are unnecessary if source control is adequate. Biliary specimens collected during surgery should be sent for culture.

complicated-cholecystitis.name: Complicated cholecystitis

primary_therapy.adjunct: +/- gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h (in critically ill patients)

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h + amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h

complicated-cholecystitis.comments: If the patient is in sepsis or septic shock, consider starting a carbapenem empirically. Contact microbiologist if the patient is immunocompromised or had recent antibiotic exposure.

acute-cholangitis.source_control: Source control with adequate biliary drainage will shorten the antibiotic duration

cefotaxime 2g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

acute-cholangitis.comments: Source control with adequate biliary drainage will shorten the antibiotic duration. Send bile for culture and ABST. Contact microbiologist if the patient is immunocompromised or had recent antibiotic exposure.

biliary-sepsis-or-healthcare-associated-.name: Biliary sepsis or healthcare-associated biliary infection of any severity

primary_therapy.adjunct: +/- metronidazole 500mg IV q8h +/- teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h 3 doses followed by 400mg IV q24h
+/- metronidazole 500mg IV q8h +/- teicoplanin 400mg IV q12h 3 doses followed by 400mg IV q24h

diverticulitis-mild.name: Diverticulitis - mild
diverticulitis-mild.presentation: Localized sigmoid wall thickening / pericolic fat stranding

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 500mg PO q12h + metronidazole 400mg PO q8h

diverticulitis-moderate-to-severe.name: Diverticulitis - moderate to severe
diverticulitis-moderate-to-severe.source_control: Drainage of abscess is necessary along with antibiotic therapy

primary_therapy.dose: ceftriaxone 2g IV q24h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
cefotaxime 2g IV q8h + metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h
