amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

diverticulitis-moderate-to-severe.comments: Drainage of abscess is necessary along with antibiotic therapy. If the patient is in sepsis or septic shock, consider starting a carbapenem empirically. Contact microbiologist.

pyogenic-liver-abscess.name: Pyogenic liver abscess

primary_therapy.dose: ceftriaxone 2g IV q24h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h
cefotaxime 1g IV q8h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h

pyogenic-liver-abscess.comments: Melioidosis needs to be excluded. Aspirate should be sent for Gram stain, aerobic/anaerobic bacterial culture, testing for fungal and mycobacterial pathogens. Entamoeba histolytica should be considered based on epidemiologic factors.

acute-pancreatitis-severe-infected-necro.name: Acute pancreatitis - severe pancreatitis/ infected pancreatic necrosis

primary_therapy.dose: 500 mg IV q6h (in critically ill patient)

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h + gentamicin 5mg/kg IV q24h

acute-pancreatitis-severe-infected-necro.comments: Prophylactic antibiotics are not recommended. Antimicrobial therapy is best indicated for culture-proven infection in pancreatic necrosis or when infection is strongly suspected (gas in the collection, bacteraemia, sepsis or clinical deterioration). Patients with 30% or more of necrosis are at a greater risk of developing infection.

spontaneous-bacterial-peritonitis.name: Peritonitis - spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) / primary peritonitis
spontaneous-bacterial-peritonitis.presentation: In SBP, bacterial infection in ascitic fluid is present without any intra-abdominal surgically treatable source of infection
spontaneous-bacterial-peritonitis.comments: SBP is very common in patients with cirrhosis and ascites. Ascitic fluid should be sent for culture & ABST. Levofloxacin is a "Reserve Category" antibiotic (Annex 01). Contact microbiologist.

secondary-bacterial-peritonitis.name: Peritonitis - secondary bacterial peritonitis
secondary-bacterial-peritonitis.presentation: Perforation of bowel and diverticula or post-operative peritonitis
secondary-bacterial-peritonitis.source_control: Early surgical source control and antibiotic therapy is required

primary_therapy.dose: 500mg IV q6h (in critically ill patient with sepsis or septic shock)
1g IV q8h (in critically ill patient with sepsis or septic shock)

alternative_therapy.dose: ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h + metronidazole 500mg IV q8h + amikacin 15mg/kg IV q24h

secondary-bacterial-peritonitis.comments: Early surgical source control and antibiotic therapy is required. Inability to control the septic source is associated with a very high mortality rate. Ascitic fluid should be sent for culture. Empirical anti MRSA and antifungal therapy is generally not indicated unless patient has risk factors. Contact microbiologist.

peritoneal-dialysis-peritonitis-moderate.name: Peritonitis related to peritoneal dialysis - moderate

primary_therapy.dose: Intra peritoneal intermittent dosing: vancomycin 15-30mg/kg every 5-7days + ceftazidime 1-1.5g daily

Intra peritoneal continuous dosing: vancomycin loading dose of 20-25mg/kg followed by a maintenance dose of 25mg/L in all exchanges + ceftazidime loading dose of 500mg/L followed by a maintenance dose of 125mg/L

alternative_therapy.dose: Intra peritoneal intermittent dosing: vancomycin 15-30mg/kg every 5-7days + gentamicin 0.6 mg/kg daily (gentamicin is not recommended for continuous dosing)

peritoneal-dialysis-peritonitis-moderate.comments: Send blood and other relevant specimens for culture. Vancomycin and ceftazidime can be mixed in the dialysis fluid of the same dialysis bag. Do not mix vancomycin and ceftazidime in a syringe or in an empty peritoneal dialysis fluid bag. If facilities are not available for measurement of serum vancomycin levels, vancomycin treatment should be monitored with serum creatinine. Timing of intermittent dosing depends on trough level of vancomycin. (repeat dose when trough level is 15mg/ml) Adjust doses according to renal functions. In intermittent dosing, the antibiotic-containing dialysis solution must be allowed to dwell for at least 6 hours to allow adequate absorption of the antibiotic into the systemic circulation. Contact microbiologist.

peritoneal-dialysis-peritonitis-severe.name: Peritonitis related to peritoneal dialysis - severe

primary_therapy.dose: vancomycin 1g IV q12h + ceftazidime 1g IV q8h
primary_therapy.adjunct: In addition to above intra peritoneal antibiotics

alternative_therapy.dose: vancomycin 1g IV q12h + ciprofloxacin 400mg IV q12h
alternative_therapy.adjunct: In addition to above intra peritoneal antibiotics
